## ★THE TARGET — all 500 trajectories at 100% each

**Ian, 2026-08-31: _"we have to finished all 200 trajectories to each 100%, put it to our roadmap"_ —
and later the same day, the exhaustive expansion: the program is now T1–T500, and the target spans all
of it.** `.momentum_drive` stays armed for this program.

That is the standing objective, written here rather than left in a session transcript so every future
session reads it before anything else.

**What 100% MEANS, stated so it cannot be reached by flattery.** The registry's pct is fixed per status
(`specced 5 · walked 25 · fixed 60 · locked 100`), so **100% is `locked`, and nothing else** — and
`tools/validate_trajectory_registry.py` holds `locked` to naming **at least one gate that is registered
in `run_platform_checks.py`**. A trajectory therefore cannot reach 100% by editing a number: it needs a
gate that actually runs on the board. "All 500 at 100%" is exactly **"all 500 locked, each with a
registered, running gate."**

**Where the program stands is ALWAYS the generated scoreboard above — never a count typed here** (a
hand-typed table drifted against the header within a week of being written; the generated block cannot).
Structurally the distance decomposes as:

- **locked** — done; nothing to re-earn while its gates stay green on the board.
- **locking** — gate built; finish the row's own `Remaining:` line, then lock. The cheapest closures.
- **fixing** — the genuine build queue of the original 200.
- **walked** — capstones sequenced last by design (T196, T200).
- **specced** — the T201–T500 expansion catalog: honest 5% until each is actually walked.

**The pct-weighted headline must not be read as progress toward this target.** The doctrine's own rule
applies to this very number: one metric at a comfortable value while the axis Ian named — *every*
trajectory at 100% — is measured only by the locked count. Adding the 300 expansion arcs correctly
DROPPED the headline; a header that cannot drop cannot be honest.

**The honest sequencing, from the 62 `locking` rows' own `Remaining:` lines:**
- **1** (`T179`) is waiting on the wave-close **re-earn only** — it closes when the restamp lands.
- **57** carry real, named remaining work — the cheapest distance to 100%, because each already has its
  gate built and sits at 72–99%.
- **4** carry no `Remaining:` line and need their state re-read before they can be claimed either way.

`WAVE_CLOSE_QUEUE.md` (generated) holds every one of those remainder lines; it is the work list for this
target, not a summary of it.

## ★THE TARGET, EXTENDED — the vehicle waves + the 102-dim rubric critique (Ian, 2026-09-03)

**Ian, 2026-09-03, put here strictly so we stay aligned on what "finished" means.** The program grew
again this day: the vehicle-seed extension added **VD (15 real-document extraction rows)** and **VP
(200 production-page deepwalk rows)** on top of the 500 + VM(10). The target is unchanged in KIND —
**100% still means `locked`, and nothing else** — and now spans all of it.

**Where the new waves actually stand (the generated scoreboard above is the SSOT; this prose must not
contradict it).** As of 2026-09-03 the split by family is:

- **Base 500 (T1–T500):** 474 `locked` · 6 `locking` · 20 `descoped` (org-federation tier, deliberately out of scope).
- **VM (vehicle lane, 10):** 10 `locked` — finished.
- **VD (real-document extraction, 15):** 0 `locked` · 15 `locking` — built + walked live against 11 real online documents + all format paths; awaiting the board to lock.
- **VP (production deepwalk, 200):** 0 `locked` · 200 `locking` — walked live once (in-motion lens) as each cell's persona × device, findings fixed live; awaiting the board to lock.

**So NONE of the 200 new VP rows, and none of the 15 VD rows, are `finished` yet — they are `locking`
(built, one gate named), not `locked`.** The pct-weighted headline (~97%) counts a `locking` row at 90;
it must NOT be read as "done." A row crosses `locking → locked` ONLY when the full board runs and
confirms its named gate is green (`tools/post_board_promote.py --apply`) — that is Ian's ~6h gate.

**★THE 102-DIM RUBRIC CRITIQUE IS A NAMED TARGET (Ian, 2026-09-03: _"you have to do also the 102-dim,
don't be lazy"_).** The first-pass VP walk graded each row against the single IN-MOTION lens; that is
NOT the finish line. The deepwalk's full deliverable is grading **every in-scope trajectory against the
full UFAI UI/UX rubric — 33 classes / 102 dimensions (`ufai-rubric-spec.json`)** — recording per-dim
verdicts + findings in `critic_registry.json`, fixing what surfaces, and locking each row on a gate that
runs on the board. A VP/VD row is not `locked` until (a) its 102-dim critique is recorded and (b) its
gate is green on the board. `.momentum_drive` stays armed for this until every in-scope trajectory is
`locked` with a full-rubric critique behind it.

### Wave W — Security & adversarial personas (T361–T384, 24)
- **T361** · BOLA: guess another hive's asset id — _adversary enumerates /rest/v1/assets?id=<other-hive> hoping the ref, not RLS, is the only guard_
- **T362** · Broken function-level auth: worker hits admin RPC — _signed-in worker calls an owner-only RPC directly, betting the button was the only gate_
- **T363** · JWT-in-body trust — _attacker sends a claim in the request body hoping an edge function trusts it over the verified JWT_
- **T364** · Tenant boundary via forged hive_id — _attacker posts a write with someone else's hive_id to cross the tenant wall_
- **T365** · Mass assignment on profile update — _attacker adds role:owner to a profile PATCH hoping the column is unguarded_
- **T366** · IDOR on marketplace order — _buyer edits an order id in the URL to read a stranger's transaction and address_
- **T367** · Stored XSS in a logbook entry — _attacker plants <script> in free text hoping a consumer renders it unescaped_
- **T368** · SQL/PostgREST injection via filter param — _attacker crafts a filter operator to widen a query past its intended row set_
- **T369** · SSRF via a webhook/callback URL — _attacker points an outbound integration URL at an internal address_
- **T370** · Rate-limit / brute force on login — _attacker scripts the login edge function to credential-stuff_
- **T371** · Password-reset token reuse — _attacker replays a supervisor-reset-password token after it should have burned_
- **T372** · Enumerate users via signup error deltas — _attacker distinguishes 'exists' from 'created' by response timing/text_
- **T373** · Invite-code forgery / replay — _attacker crafts or reuses a hive invite code to self-join_
- **T374** · Privilege escalation via stale membership — _removed member's cached session still writes before the wall catches up_
- **T375** · File-upload content smuggling — _attacker uploads a mislabeled file to a storage bucket to bypass a MIME gate_
- **T376** · Signed-URL scope abuse — _attacker widens or reuses a storage signed URL past its object_
- **T377** · CSRF on a state-changing GET — _attacker tricks a session into a cross-site state change on a non-idempotent endpoint_
- **T378** · Webhook signature bypass (gcash-receipt-inbound) — _attacker posts a forged payment webhook without a valid signature to mark a txn paid_
- **T379** · Race to double-spend a marketplace credit — _attacker fires two concurrent redemptions of the same credit_
- **T380** · Exfil via export-hive-data as a low-role — _low-privilege member triggers a full-hive export they should not receive_
- **T381** · Prompt injection into an AI agent — _attacker plants instructions in user content that an AI orchestrator later executes_
- **T382** · Denial-of-wallet on a metered AI endpoint — _attacker loops an expensive AI call to exhaust the owner's budget_
- **T383** · Open redirect on return-url params — _attacker crafts ?return= to bounce a signed-in user to a phishing origin_
- **T384** · Audit-log tampering / gap — _attacker performs an action on a path that writes no audit row, hiding the trail_

### Wave X — Accessibility spectrum (T385–T402, 18)
- **T385** · Screen-reader: complete a work order end-to-end — _a blind supervisor drives logbook->assign with NVDA/VoiceOver, intent = finish without sight_
- **T386** · Keyboard-only: no mouse anywhere — _a motor-impaired user tabs through every interactive control, focus never trapped or lost_
- **T387** · Low-vision at 400% zoom — _a partially-sighted user zooms to 400%; no content clipped, no horizontal scroll trap_
- **T388** · Color-blind: status conveyed beyond hue — _a deuteranope reads asset health where red/green alone would be ambiguous_
- **T389** · Switch-access single-input navigation — _a quadriplegic user drives the app with one switch and scanning_
- **T390** · Voice-control (Dragon/Voice Access) — _a user speaks 'click Assign' — every control has a spoken-accessible name_
- **T391** · Screen-magnifier follow-focus — _a low-vision user's magnifier follows focus and new content into the viewport_
- **T392** · Deaf/HoH: captions & no audio-only cues — _a Deaf user needs every audio alert mirrored visually (voice-journal playback captioned)_
- **T393** · Cognitive load: plain-language + steps — _a user with a cognitive disability needs a long form chunked and jargon explained_
- **T394** · Reduced-motion respected — _a vestibular-disorder user with prefers-reduced-motion sees no parallax/auto-animation_
- **T395** · Reflow at 320 CSS px (WCAG 1.4.10) — _content reflows to a single column at 320px with no loss of function_
- **T396** · Focus-visible on every control — _a keyboard user always sees where focus is; no invisible focus ring_
- **T397** · Form errors announced to AT — _a validation error is programmatically associated and announced, not just colored_
- **T398** · Live-region for async updates — _a screen-reader user hears a toast/status change via an aria-live region_
- **T399** · Touch target >=44px on phone — _a user with a tremor can hit every phone control without mis-tapping a neighbor_
- **T400** · Skip-link & landmark navigation — _a screen-reader user jumps past nav to main via a skip link and landmarks_
- **T401** · High-contrast / forced-colors mode — _a Windows High Contrast user retains all borders, icons and state_
- **T402** · Timeout & session-extend accessible — _a slow user is warned before a session/auto-save timeout and can extend it_

### Wave Y — New human personas (T403–T420, 18)
- **T403** · DOLE labor inspector reviews compliance — _a government inspector audits permit-to-work and shift records for a Philippine plant_
- **T404** · Insurance assessor verifies maintenance history — _an assessor needs tamper-evident asset maintenance history for a claim_
- **T405** · Procurement officer evaluates a marketplace seller — _a corporate buyer vets a seller's trust signals before a bulk order_
- **T406** · Night-shift lone operator — _a solo night-shift tech logs a fault at 3am with no supervisor online_
- **T407** · Regional manager across many hives — _a multi-site manager compares OEE across the hives they oversee_
- **T408** · Brand-new trainee, day one — _a fresh hire with zero context is onboarded into a hive and their first task_
- **T409** · Contractor working across multiple hives — _an external contractor switches between three client hives without data bleed_
- **T410** · External auditor with read-only, time-boxed access — _an ISO auditor gets scoped, expiring read access to evidence_
- **T411** · Finance controller reconciles marketplace payouts — _a controller ties GCash payouts to completed orders for the books_
- **T412** · Plant safety officer runs an incident review — _a safety officer reconstructs an incident from logbook + audit trail_
- **T413** · HR verifies a worker's skill matrix — _HR confirms certifications before assigning a regulated task_
- **T414** · Vendor/OEM support engineer — _an equipment vendor is granted a narrow window to diagnose one asset_
- **T415** · Executive on a quarterly board review — _a non-technical exec reads the platform's headline reliability KPIs_
- **T416** · Union representative checks fair scheduling — _a rep audits shift assignments for equity across workers_
- **T417** · Data-protection officer handles a subject request — _a DPO fulfils a GDPR/PDPA export/erasure request for one worker_
- **T418** · Retiring supervisor hands over a hive — _an outgoing supervisor transfers ownership and knowledge before leaving_
- **T419** · Seasonal surge temp worker — _a temp is added for a shutdown, works two weeks, is cleanly offboarded_
- **T420** · Regulator cross-checks a public tools claim — _a standards body verifies a public calculator matches the cited standard_

### Wave Z — Data pathology deep (T421–T438, 18)
- **T421** · Partial write: order paid, fulfilment row missing — _a half-committed transaction leaves the UI asserting a state the data denies_
- **T422** · Orphaned child after parent delete — _an asset is deleted but its work orders survive, pointing at nothing_
- **T423** · Timezone-crossing shift at midnight — _a shift spanning midnight in Asia/Manila is counted in the wrong day_
- **T424** · Float precision in a cost/hours rollup — _accumulated rounding drifts a financial total the user can check by hand_
- **T425** · Migration half-state as UX — _a user hits a page mid-migration where old and new columns disagree_
- **T426** · Duplicate rows from a double-submit — _a retried POST creates two identical records the list now shows twice_
- **T427** · Null-vs-zero conflation in a metric — _a missing reading is averaged as 0, deflating an availability number_
- **T428** · Stale cache after a write — _a user saves, navigates, and sees the pre-save value from a warm cache_
- **T429** · Unicode/emoji in names breaks a render — _a worker named with non-Latin script or emoji breaks a downstream label_
- **T430** · Very long text overflows every container — _a 10k-character logbook note must not break layout or truncate silently_
- **T431** · Clock skew between client and server — _a client with a wrong clock stamps events out of order_
- **T432** · Soft-deleted row leaks into an aggregate — _a soft-deleted asset still counts in a hive's totals_
- **T433** · Enum drift: a status value no code handles — _a legacy status value renders as a blank chip nobody planned for_
- **T434** · Cross-hive id collision in a shared table — _two hives' sequences collide in a table keyed without the hive_
- **T435** · Large dataset pagination correctness — _a hive with 50k assets pages without dropping or repeating rows_
- **T436** · Currency/precision at scale (centavos) — _GCash amounts in centavos survive rollup without a rounding leak_
- **T437** · Backfill leaves created_at in the future — _an import sets timestamps ahead of now, breaking 'recent' ordering_
- **T438** · Referential repair crosses the tenant boundary — _an automated fix touches a sibling hive's row — the boundary must hold_

### Wave AA — Financial & economic edge (T439–T454, 16)
- **T439** · Refund after a completed marketplace order — _a buyer disputes; the refund path must reverse credit and ledger cleanly_
- **T440** · Chargeback / reversed GCash payment — _a payment reverses post-fulfilment; the platform reconciles both sides_
- **T441** · Currency & tax on a cross-region sale — _a sale spanning tax jurisdictions computes the right line items_
- **T442** · AI credit exhausted mid-transaction — _an owner's AI budget runs out halfway through a multi-step agent run_
- **T443** · Fraud ring: coordinated fake reviews — _multiple colluding accounts inflate a seller's trust signals_
- **T444** · GCash webhook arrives late / out of order — _a delayed payment webhook lands after the timeout; state reconciles_
- **T445** · Double-charge on a retried checkout — _a network retry must not charge the buyer twice_
- **T446** · Payout to a since-deleted seller account — _a payout is owed to a seller who closed their account_
- **T447** · Price change mid-cart — _a listing's price changes between add-to-cart and checkout_
- **T448** · Subscription proration on plan change — _an owner upgrades mid-cycle; the invoice prorates correctly_
- **T449** · Negative-balance / overdraw guard — _a credit spend that would go negative is refused, not silently allowed_
- **T450** · Escrow release dispute — _buyer and seller disagree on delivery; escrow holds until resolved_
- **T451** · Tax-exempt / invoice-only buyer — _a corporate buyer needs an official receipt and tax handling_
- **T452** · Failed payout retry & idempotency — _a failed payout retries without paying twice_
- **T453** · Promo/discount stacking abuse — _a buyer stacks incompatible promos to underpay_
- **T454** · Financial report reconciles to the ledger — _the analytics revenue figure equals the sum of ledger rows, provably_

### Wave AB — Federation & multi-org (T455–T470, 16)
- **T455** · Parent org rolls up child-hive metrics — _a corporate parent aggregates KPIs across subsidiary hives it owns_
- **T456** · Cross-hive contractor with scoped access — _a contractor sees only the assets each client hive shared, nothing else_
- **T457** · Data-sharing agreement between two hives — _two independent hives share a defined slice under an agreement_
- **T458** · Org-level RBAC above hive roles — _an org admin role spans hives without becoming owner of each_
- **T459** · Subsidiary spins off into its own org — _a child hive is cleanly detached into an independent org with its data_
- **T460** · Shared marketplace seller across hives — _one seller identity operates from several hives without leaking between them_
- **T461** · Central template pushed to all child hives — _a parent publishes a PM template every subsidiary inherits_
- **T462** · Cross-org benchmarking, anonymized — _hives compare against an anonymized peer benchmark without exposing rows_
- **T463** · Merge two hives into one — _an acquisition merges two hives' assets and members without collision_
- **T464** · Federated single sign-on across orgs — _a user with an org SSO identity enters the right hives_
- **T465** · Delegated admin: parent acts for a child — _a parent admin performs an action in a child hive, audited as delegated_
- **T466** · Billing consolidated at the org level — _subsidiaries' usage rolls into one org invoice_
- **T467** · Cross-hive asset transfer — _an asset moves from one hive to another with its history intact_
- **T468** · Region-partitioned data residency — _an org keeps PH and non-PH hive data in the right residency_
- **T469** · Org-wide policy overrides a hive setting — _an org security policy forces a setting a hive cannot loosen_
- **T470** · Guest hive with an expiry date — _a temporary partner hive auto-expires and revokes access on the date_

### Wave AC — Platform-evolution & longitudinal (T471–T484, 14)
- **T471** · Deprecation-as-UX: a retired page's callers — _a user follows an old link to a retired page and is guided forward, not 404'd_
- **T472** · Version-skew client after a deploy — _a user on a stale tab hits new APIs; the app detects and reloads gracefully_
- **T473** · Breaking-change migration a live user is in — _a schema change lands while a user has a half-filled form open_
- **T474** · Multi-year asset history renders — _an asset with five years of records loads and charts without choking_
- **T475** · A feature flag flips mid-session — _a flag toggles while a user is mid-flow; the UI stays coherent_
- **T476** · Old cached service worker serves stale app — _a returning PWA user gets the new version, not a months-old cache_
- **T477** · Data written by a retired feature — _rows created by a since-removed feature still render safely_
- **T478** · Long-dormant account returns — _a user absent a year signs in to a changed platform and re-orients_
- **T479** · Renamed field across an API version — _a field renamed between versions maps for old and new clients_
- **T480** · Historical report reproducibility — _a report run today for last quarter matches what it said then_
- **T481** · Bulk re-embed after a model upgrade — _an embedding model change triggers a backfill without downtime_
- **T482** · Sunset an integration with active users — _a CMMS connector is retired while hives still use it; they're migrated_
- **T483** · Config/default change is backward-safe — _a changed default doesn't silently alter existing hives' behavior_
- **T484** · Terms/consent re-acceptance flow — _a policy update requires re-consent without locking users out of their data_

### Wave AE — Compound systemic failures (T493–T500, 8)
- **T493** · DB failover mid-write storm — _the primary fails over while many hives are writing; no lost or dup rows_
- **T494** · Edge-function cold-start cascade under load — _a traffic spike cold-starts many functions at once; the queue holds_
- **T495** · Auth outage with cached sessions active — _the auth service is down but signed-in users must degrade safely_
- **T496** · Storage unavailable during an upload wave — _object storage blips while uploads are in flight; they retry, none corrupt_
- **T497** · Realtime + REST disagree during a partition — _a network partition splits realtime from REST; the UI reconciles on heal_
- **T498** · Third-party (GCash) outage mid-checkout — _the payment provider is down during checkouts; orders park, none half-pay_
- **T499** · Cron/scheduled-agents backlog after downtime — _scheduled jobs pile up during an outage and drain without double-firing_
- **T500** · Region-wide degradation, graceful global — _one region degrades; the platform stays coherent for everyone else_

Run against the standing FAIL list. The theme: most reds were the INSTRUMENT, and the one real
defect was invisible to every gate because the two copies of the truth agreed with each other.

| 1 | **T11, found AFTER its lock.** One ledger row `restock +4` recorded `qty_after 6` on a shelf holding 6 — 4 units invisible (shelf 10, system 6). `trg_inventory_sync_balance` mirrors `qty_after` onto `qty_on_hand`, so it guarantees the copies AGREE, never that either is RIGHT; the wrong total was canonised as the balance. Producer = inventory.html's fallback lane, chosen by `if (HIVE_ID && navigator.onLine)` — a false-negative `onLine` takes the client read-modify-write branch while the INSERT still succeeds, bypassing `inventory_restock`'s atomic `FOR UPDATE`. T11's four recorded fixes all walk the DEDUCT direction; restock was never walked | row repaired (6→10, balance mirrored); migration `20260828000006` derives `qty_after` for relative movements (`use`/`restock`/`add`), leaves absolute `adjustment` authoritative, and SKIPS backdated inserts so a seeder replaying history is not rewritten. One DB fix covers both client lanes (1774 use + 1889 restock) | `inventory-ledger-reconciled` green; **4 behaviours proven, cleanup exact**: a wrong relative total is corrected (999→15) · a CORRECT one is a no-op (10+3=13 stored verbatim, so `inventory_restock`'s atomic path is untouched) · a backdated insert keeps its own number (777) so a seeder replaying history is never rewritten · an absolute `adjustment` stays authoritative (42). **A defect in the FIX itself, caught by reading the gate's own ordering:** the gate chains with `lag(qty_after) OVER (ORDER BY created_at, id)`, while my predecessor took the greatest key among `created_at <= NEW.created_at` — so on a same-transaction timestamp TIE (the MR4 shape, now() is fixed) it could chain a row off a sibling the gate sorts AFTER it. Now compares the full `(created_at, id)` key, matching the gate exactly; the residual bulk-tie case is documented in the migration as deliberately out of scope (a BEFORE trigger cannot see rows that do not exist yet, and it is still strictly better: the tail row is corrected where previously both kept the bad value) |

**And the lever WORKS where the property is real: one row converted, permanently.**
`one_brief_per_day` ("an AMC briefing is one per hive per shift_date") is pure DB truth, enforced by
`uq_amc_briefings_hive_shift`. Built `tools/psql_probes/alert-hub__one_brief_per_day.sql` in the house style
and it PASSES all six assertions: the unique index exists · **68 groups checked** (non-vacuity printed, so an
empty table cannot masquerade as agreement) · 0 duplicate days · a second brief for a taken hive+date is
REFUSED with 23505 · a control insert for the SAME hive on a free date is ACCEPTED (teeth the other way -
what separates a working uniqueness rule from a table that rejects everything) · and the count is restored
after rollback, so no residue. Two bugs of my own on the way, both caught by running it rather than reasoning
about it: `brief` is a JSON column and I passed a bare string, so the "duplicate refused" teeth silently never
fired - the fix reuses the live row's own brief, which is self-grounding anyway. **That row never needs a
browser again.** The 87 remaining CD-invariant rows are now a known, sized conversion queue rather than an
**A second row converted the same way:** `asset-hub__hierarchy_acyclic` ("a node cannot become its own ancestor") - 96 nodes walked by recursive CTE, 0 cyclic paths. Nothing in the schema REFUSES a cycle (a parent_id cycle is not expressible as a CHECK), so there the guard is the DETECTOR, not the database - its teeth mint a real cycle from a live parent/child pair inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK and require it to be SEEN. Both probes verified to leave zero residue (96 nodes / 0 cycles, 68 briefings / 0 probe rows).
**A third:** `asset-hub__rpn_recomputed` ("RPN equals S x O x D exactly, recomputed rather than trusted from a stored column that can drift") - 300 modes, 0 disagreements, and the strongest answer was already in the schema: `rpn` is GENERATED ALWAYS, so the drift this oracle exists to catch is structurally impossible rather than merely absent. Asserted anyway, because a later migration could drop the generation and leave a plain column that silently accepts anything while every row still read correct on the day it changed - so its teeth require Postgres to REFUSE a hand-written RPN ("can only be updated to DEFAULT ... is a generated column"; my first regex guessed the INSERT wording and the teeth silently never fired until I read the real error). 300 modes intact afterwards.
**A fourth:** `asset-hub__delete_orphans_nothing` - an orphan here is invisible (the node leaves the tree while its FMEA modes and sensor readings sit in the tables forever, counted by every aggregate that does not join back to a node). It asserts TWO separate claims on purpose: **13 FKs reference asset_nodes and 0 lack an explicit delete rule** (so a new child table cannot quietly arrive with NO ACTION and start orphaning), AND that the rules actually FIRE - a live node with 4 FMEA children is deleted inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK and the children must be gone in the same transaction. Rule-declared and rule-works are different claims; both are checked. **A fifth:** `community__xp_once_and_reverses`. Reading `trg_community_post_xp` first showed WHY it is worth pinning: the trigger does not defend the once-only rule in application logic - it writes `community_post_xp_awards (post_id, reason)` with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and increments XP only when that insert actually CLAIMED a row (`GET DIAGNOSTICS claimed = ROW_COUNT`). So the guarantee IS the unique key: if it goes, a replayed trigger silently pays twice and nothing else notices. 20 awards, 0 duplicate pairs, a replayed claim REFUSED with 23505, a free (post, reason) pair ACCEPTED.

**A sixth, and it taught the day's recurring lesson a THIRD time:** `engineering-design__delete_respects_links`. Projects link to calcs through `project_links (link_type, link_id)` - POLYMORPHIC, so no foreign key and no delete rule - and my first read of that concluded "unenforced, holds by luck" and I wrote a probe whose teeth asserted a delete WOULD dangle. It didn't: the link vanished with the calc. `trg_cleanup_project_links` does the work, and **a foreign key cannot express a polymorphic reference**, so a trigger is the RIGHT mechanism here, not a missing one. Same shape as whSignInWall and the headers const: a guard I had not looked for, read as a guard that was not there. The probe now asserts the trigger AND keeps `enforced_by_foreign_key | f` deliberately, so the day someone adds a real FK that line changes and gets noticed.

**A seventh, and it closes the loop on this morning's inventory defect:** `inventory__no_negative_stock`. There is NO CHECK constraint on `qty_on_hand` - the guarantee lives entirely in `inventory_deduct`, which computes `GREATEST(0, v_qty - p_qty)`. So the probe CALLS it rather than grepping for GREATEST (a comment or a renamed helper would read identically), and it calls it **as a real member** assumed from a live `hive_members` row, because the RPC is SECURITY DEFINER and re-checks membership - running as postgres would bypass the very path under test. Asking for 9,999 more than the shelf holds leaves the balance at 0, never negative, and - the assertion that matters - **the ledger records what ACTUALLY left, not what was asked**. That is the same class as the restock row repaired this morning: a movement the shelf could not make must never appear as one it did. Two wrong assumptions of mine on the way, both caught by running it: the RPC returns the NEW quantity rather than the moved amount, and `stock_conserved` was dropped as redundant once I checked - the `inventory-ledger-reconciled` gate already asserts it.

**An eighth:** `pm-scheduler__one_completion_one_mirror` - the "not two" half is a DATABASE guarantee: `pm_completions_dedup_uidx` is a PARTIAL unique index on (scope_item_id, worker_name, (completed_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date) WHERE scope_item_id IS NOT NULL, so a double-tap, a refresh-mid-submit or a replayed request cannot pay twice for the same scope item on the same day. The probe HONOURS that partial predicate in its duplicate count rather than ignoring it - counting rows the index does not cover would report duplicates the guarantee never claimed to prevent, which is the oracle-vocabulary error this bank keeps designing against. 1,597 completions, 0 same-day duplicates, a replay REFUSED, the same pair on another day ACCEPTED.

**A ninth:** `project-manager__no_orphans_on_archive` - 6 FKs reference projects, none without an explicit delete rule, and a live project with **19 children** deleted inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK leaves zero behind. Its child count is taken from the CATALOG rather than a list written into the probe, so a seventh child table added tomorrow is covered without editing it - the same reason the FK-presence claim is asserted separately from the FK-fires claim: a schema can pass the first and fail the second after a table is rebuilt.

**A tenth:** `pm-scheduler__scope_bound` - a completion carries its own `asset_id` AND a `scope_item_id`, and if those disagree the tick was filed against a machine the scope item does not belong to, so every compliance figure that groups by asset counts it under the wrong one, silently and forever. The FK forces the scope item to EXIST; a cross-table agreement between two asset_ids is not expressible as a CHECK, so the guard is the DETECTOR and the teeth mint a real mismatch and require it seen. `hive_id` agreement is checked alongside `asset_id`, because a completion filed under the wrong HIVE is the tenancy version of the same defect. 1,597 completions, 0 mismatches on both axes.

**An eleventh:** `project-manager__links_tenant_bound` - `project_links` is polymorphic, so NO foreign key can carry tenancy and the link table is exactly where it is easiest to lose: one wrong link_id renders another hive's asset, logbook entry or completion on a project page with no error anywhere. The probe resolves EACH link_type against its OWN table and compares to the project's hive, rather than trusting `project_links.hive_id` - the link row's own column agreeing proves the ROW is filed correctly, not that the thing it POINTS AT belongs here, and only the second is the oracle. 54 links across 5 domains, 0 cross-hive; teeth mint a real cross-hive link and require it seen.

**ELEVEN converted, all passing together, zero residue** (txns 454 / pm 1,597 / projects 12 / calcs 30 / nodes 96 all at baseline afterwards). Queue SIZED rather than guessed: of 84 distinct CD-invariant oracles, **59 are DB-only shaped and 25 are mixed** - the mixed ones name a UI fact as well (a chart's rendered series, a page break, "the surface says which"), which is exactly WHY they are live-walk and why they should stay that way. So the convertible queue is ~47, not 84. And even that is an upper bound: `xp_is_ledger_sum` is DB-only in SHAPE yet provably unprovable (the fire-and-forget ledger above), so each candidate still needs the property verified before a probe is written. `aggregate_tenant_bound` was skipped for the opposite reason - a `hive-isolation` gate already backs 132 rows, and converting it without a no-redundancy check would duplicate coverage rather than add it.

**The conversion exercise is AUDITING the oracles, and two have already failed that audit.** Writing a probe forces the property to be stated in SQL, and that is where a claim nobody could check gets checked. (1) `xp_is_ledger_sum` asserts conservation the code explicitly declines to provide (`EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL` around the ledger write). (2) `reaction_count_distinct` asserts *"one person cannot react twice to one post"* while the unique index is on **(post_id, worker_name, emoji)** - the same person reacting twice with different emojis is permitted BY CONSTRUCTION; and with **1 row in the whole table** a probe would pass vacuously anyway, the exact failure the non-vacuity rail exists to stop. Neither was silently re-specced: a row whose ORACLE is wrong needs the claim fixed, and that is Ian's call, not a quiet edit buried in a probe.

**Three distinct reasons a candidate is NOT convertible, all met in practice - which is why the queue must be walked, not batch-converted.** (1) The oracle asserts what the code declines to provide (`xp_is_ledger_sum`). (2) The population is too small for the assertion to mean anything - `reaction_count_distinct` has 1 reaction row, and `plan_links_not_duplicates` has **228 schedule items of which 0 carry a `logbook_ref`**, so a probe would pass over an empty set, the exact vacuity the non-vacuity rail exists to stop. (3) An existing gate already covers it (`aggregate_tenant_bound` vs the `hive-isolation` gate's 132 rows). Each of these is only visible by MEASURING first; none is visible from the oracle text.
undifferentiated walk - and the xp_is_ledger_sum result above is the discipline that goes with it: convert
only where the property is actually true.

**Trying to convert ONE of those CD-invariant rows found an oracle that cannot be true.**
`PB-achievements-055-CD-invariant-xp_is_ledger_sum` asserts *"the XP total equals the sum of
achievement_xp_log"* - textbook ledger-conservation, and exactly the shape a psql recipe should own. Measured
first: **45 of 58 (worker, achievement) pairs disagree**, with totals like 349,455 against a ledger of 95 from
a single entry. My first query was wrong and I caught it (`worker_achievements` is one row PER ACHIEVEMENT,
72 rows / 20 workers, so a per-worker join was a category error) - but the correct grain still disagreed.
**The reason is in `award_achievement_xp` itself:** it upserts `xp_total = xp_total + p_xp`, then writes the
ledger row inside `BEGIN ... EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL; END`, commented *"fire-and-forget: failure is
acceptable, never block the action"*. So the balance moves while the ledger entry may silently never exist -
by design. **The oracle asserts a property the implementation explicitly declines to provide**, which is why
it can only ever be hand-walked: no probe can prove it, and any probe written to would be permanently red.
Same shape as the inventory mirror earlier today - a total that no ledger can audit - and the same class as
[[feedback_a_trust_claim_no_query_enforces]]. Two honest repairs, both Ian-scoped because they change what is
CLAIMED: restate the oracle to the delta that IS provable (one award writes one entry and moves the total by
exactly that amount, in a rolled-back transaction), or make the ledger write non-optional so conservation
becomes real. Not silently re-specced here - the row stays live-walk with the reason now recorded.

**The 839 interactive rows are a structured backlog, not one undifferentiated grind.** Splitting them by
category against the gate-backed set shows most categories are MIXED - `CC-failure-injection` is 237
gate-backed vs 62 hand-walked, `CN-ux-journey` 262 vs 43, `CO-ux-recovery` 143 vs 103 - so the walked rows are
the CELLS each prover does not yet reach, not a different kind of claim. Two categories are live-walk ONLY:
**CD-invariant (88)** and **CI-domain-truth (128)**. That is the roadmap's own "build the structure" lever
pointing at itself: an invariant is exactly the shape `tools/psql_probes/*.sql` already replays (74 such rows
are permanently green because they became executable recipes instead of one afternoon's hand-walk). Widening
each prover to its category's uncovered cells, and converting CD-invariant rows into psql recipes, would move
rows out of the interactive residue PERMANENTLY rather than re-walking them every edit wave. Also audited
while here: all **507 declared-na rows carry a substantive rationale** - zero bare N/As, so the silence-is-not-
coverage rail is holding.

**And the live lane had a failure the fast lane never runs — `http_envelope`, which turned out to be the
detector, not the pages.** It reported *"8 pages read a relation whose refusal is indistinguishable from
absence and carry NO session gate"* (analytics, analytics-report, asset-hub, dayplanner, hive, pm-scheduler,
project-manager, skillmatrix). Every one of those pages gates — via **`whSignInWall(...)`**, 1-3 call sites
each. The gate's pattern only knew the PRE-CENTRALISATION spellings (`signin=1`, `whRequireAuth`,
`requireAuth(`), and T2 had moved the wall into one utils.js helper whose body is
`location.href = 'index.html?signin=1&return=' + here`. So the pages stopped containing the literal the
detector looks for, and **the refactor was reported as a regression**. Confirmed against HEAD first — neither
the working tree nor HEAD has `getUser()` on those pages, so this was never a working-tree regression — and
verified live the same day: report-sender sends an anon visitor to `?signin=1&return=report-sender.html` and
sign-in lands back on the page. Taught `GATE_RE` the current name; the gate now PASSES, naming its mechanisms
(*redirects-unauthenticated x21, settles-auth-before-reads x1*), and the widening carries teeth: a synthetic
page with NO mechanism is still caught. **A centralised mechanism is still a mechanism** — same shape as the
edge-content-type gate that could not see a headers const, and the fifth instrument fix of the day.
**Bounded, not assumed:** 7 other gates still mention the old spellings, and none is the same class - `cross_tab_identity` and `skeleton_resolves` match inside COMMENTS, `edge_fn_auth_gate` matches `requireAuth` as a SERVER-side helper name, and the g5d/return-promise provers CONSTRUCT the `?signin=1&return=` URL rather than detecting it. Checked each before touching any; the blindness was specific to this one detector.

**Wave close, measured (2026-08-28).** Editing stopped, then the close ran in its designed order:

- **Full static board re-run: 611 PASS, 3 distinct FAILs, 791s** (the pre-optimisation run of the same lane
  took 28+ minutes). The three are the substrate (fixed below), clone-debt and ai-asset-versioning - the two
  that are not mine.
- **Substrate rebuilt**: 572 chunks written, and the freshness gate now reads **all 798 chunks fresh**. Its
  drift list beforehand was exactly the files this turn touched (dayplanner, index, marketplace, the roadmap,
  the memory manifest, the migration catalog) - no surprises, nothing collateral.
- **Bank validated: PASS on 21 of 22 banks** - "every non-owed row carries typed, unexpired evidence". Nothing
  is claimed green that is not. `owed 0` and `invalid 0` everywhere.
- **And the bank is now massively STALE, which is the edit wave's designed consequence, not a defect.** Every
  page bank reads 200 scenarios / 26 green / **174 stale**; marketplace reads 877 / 27 green / **850 stale**
  and its ratchet correctly FAILS with *"green went backwards: 752 -> 27 ... re-walk, do not re-baseline."*
  This is A15/R4 working: a shared-file edit moves `sha_of(deps)`, evidence expires, and the bank says so
  rather than absorbing it. ~3,900 rows now need re-walking.
- **The re-earn IS scripted, and my first reading of it was WRONG.** All 70 psql-probe-backed rows are already
  GREEN (checked, not assumed). I then concluded the ~3,900 residue had "no scriptable path" because
  `bank_page_walk.py` only MERGES what a live MCP session produced - and stopped on that. **Checking the
  machinery refutes it.** By KIND the stale set is **2,980 gate / 839 live-walk / 507 declared-na / 74 psql**:
  the dominant share is GATE-backed, and "a gate-backed row is re-earned by RUNNING the gate"
  (`tools/bank_gate_restamp.py`). `tools/mega_cycle3.sh` is the existing driver - run each producer, restamp
  each gate against its fresh report, re-validate the whole bank. Proven on the spot: a dry-run restamp of one
  gate offered **178 rows across 21 banks, 0 refused**. Only the 839 live-walk rows need a browser session.
  The lesson is the recorded one - **check the machinery before calling anything a ceiling**; it usually exists.
- **A false-green hazard in that driver, found by using it.** `bank_gate_restamp` states plainly that it
  "checks recency, not verdicts", and `mega_cycle3.sh` calls `restamp` UNCONDITIONALLY after each producer -
  `run()` records OK/FAIL and nothing consumes it. So a producer that runs RED still writes a fresh report and
  still gets its rows stamped green; `ck_component_states` alone is 330 rows. Demonstrated live: `http_envelope`
  is currently RED and a dry run still offered all 178 of its rows. It is not in mega_cycle3's list, so that
  particular trap is not armed - but the shape is. Whether it is LIVE depends on which producers are red, which
  the full-board run now in flight will say. **Made visible rather than guessed at:** report shapes differ too
  much for a reliable generic verdict read (`component_states` and `viewport_overflow` carry `totals: null`,
  while `retry_views` carries `pass/fail` and `a11y_states` carries `failing`), so inventing a heuristic would
  trade a silent false green for a noisy false refusal. The tool now PRINTS what it did not check - *"NOT
  VERIFIED: the gate's VERDICT was not read - only that <report> is newer than the deps"* - at the moment the
  assumption is relied on. An assumption stated at the call site is a decision; the same assumption in a
  docstring is a trap.

**Own-goal worth writing down: I deleted a file a running job owned.** Tidying stray probe scripts out of
`/tmp` mid-session also removed `/tmp/wh_board.txt`, which a 28-minute board run was writing to. The run
completed and its entire output was unrecoverable. Probe hygiene is right, but scope it to files nothing is
holding open - or write to the session scratchpad in the first place, which is what the harness provides it for.

**Board runtime — two checks were costing ~15 minutes per run between them, both now fixed and both proven
equivalent before being trusted.** The board sat at 28+ minutes in its FAST lane, which is the lane meant to be
cheap. Profiling by watching wall-time against CPU-time found the two:

| Check | Was | Now | Why it was slow | Proof it still answers the same |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `migration-immutability` | ~389s (9 min observed) | **0.8s** | one `git log -- <file>` per migration x 572 files @ 609ms | 40 random migrations compared batched-vs-per-file, **0 mismatches**; same verdict (1 PASS/3 WARN/0 FAIL); empty-map fallback proven to engage |
| `audit_phantom_columns` | ~842s projected (7 min, 414 CPU-s) | **5s** | a word-boundary regex compiled PER COLUMN and run over EVERY blob: 1,887 columns x 1,877 blobs | 300 random columns compared tokenised-vs-regex, **0 mismatches**; same output (179 tables, 1,887 cols, 1,435 alive, 0 phantom) |

Neither changes what the check DECIDES - `--name-only` reports the same commits, and splitting on `[A-Za-z0-9_]+`
yields exactly the maximal runs the word-boundary regex matches, so token presence == regex match and the token
COUNT == the match count the own-migration `>= 2` rule needs. In both cases the original implementation was KEPT
(as a fallback, and as `_column_has_consumer_regex`) so the fast path has a live oracle to be checked against
rather than a comment claiming they agree.

**And the way they were FOUND generalises better than the fixes do.** Grepping for "subprocess call inside
a loop" matches **48** files here and is useless as a signal - almost all of them loop over two or three
candidates, which is fine. What separates a pathological one is the SIZE of the collection, which no grep
can see. Both were caught the same way instead: **compare wall-time against CPU-time.** 9 minutes with 4
CPU-seconds means blocking on I/O (the git subprocesses); 7 minutes with 414 CPU-seconds means real
computation in the wrong shape (the per-column regex). Profile the board, do not lint it.

**The third candidate was REFUSED after reading its regex, which is the point.** `audit_phantom_captures`
has the identical shape - a word-boundary pattern per capture name, scanned over every blob, 66 CPU-seconds -
so the same tokenisation looked like a free win. Its boundary is ASYMMETRIC though:
`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])name(?![A-Za-z0-9_])` includes a HYPHEN on the left and not on the right, so `foo` matches
inside `foo-bar` but NOT inside `data-foo`. A `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` tokeniser over-counts it (`data-foo` yields the
token `foo`); a hyphen-inclusive one under-counts it (`foo-bar` never yields `foo`). **Neither is equivalent,
and porting the columns fix by pattern-matching on shape would have silently changed the audit's answer** -
the failure mode being optimised against in the first place. I then BUILT the hyphen-aware tokeniser and measured it against the live regex before touching the file -
and it is **NOT equivalent either, for a reason the reading had missed**: the capture NAMES contain hyphens
(`intent-primary`, `f-min-qty`, `s-notes`), so a `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` tokeniser never emits them as tokens at all.
Measured: regex=7 matches, token=**0**, on 120 of 120 sampled names. Porting the columns fix here would have
zeroed the consumer count for every hyphenated capture and made LIVE captures look phantom - in a gate whose
output is used to delete things. **The 66 CPU-seconds stay.** A one-pass index for this shape needs to key on
the hyphenated names themselves, not on identifier runs; until someone builds and PROVES that, the slow
version is the correct version. Two candidates optimised, one refused twice - the refusals are the result.

**Measured backlog — `migration-immutability` is the board's bottleneck, ~6 minutes of subprocess wait.**
Caught while the board sat on it for 9 minutes with **4 seconds of CPU** — the signature of blocking on I/O,
not computing. It shells out to `git log --pretty=... -- <file>` once PER MIGRATION, and there are **572**;
one call measured **609ms** on this repo, so ~348s before the `git diff` calls for suspect files. Nothing is
wrong with what it CHECKS (immutability of already-committed migrations is exactly the right guard) - the
cost is the shape. The fix is one batched `git log --name-only` pass building the whole per-file commit map
in a single subprocess. DONE once the board moved off it (editing a guard while it executes is how one gets weakened by accident):
one `git log --name-only` pass builds the whole path -> commits map, with the original per-file call kept as a
FALLBACK, because a batch that silently returned nothing would make every migration look uncommitted and the
gate would pass vacuously - the exact false-green this repo keeps designing against. That fallback is PROVEN, not assumed: forcing the map empty makes the front door fall through to the per-file call and return the identical commit list. **Proven equivalent before
being trusted:** 40 random migrations compared batched-vs-per-file, **0 mismatches**, and the gate reaches the
same verdict (1 PASS / 3 WARN / 0 FAIL). **572 subprocesses -> 1; ~389s -> 0.8s; the gate itself 9 minutes -> 1
second.** A first attempt used a NUL record separator and wrote null bytes into the source; caught by
py_compile, reverted with `git checkout`, redone with a text sentinel.

**Operational note — a Docker restart brings back SOME containers, and the gaps surface two layers away.**
Docker Desktop stopped mid-session (all of :5000/:54321/:54322 closed). Restarting it brought the DB, auth,
kong, rest, realtime and storage back healthy — but **`supabase_edge_runtime_workhive` stayed Exited (255)**
and so did **`workhive_python_api_fwd`** (the socat that publishes the python API on host :8000, which
`glitchtip_query`, `python_api_live_invoke` and `python_api_ufai_sweep` all read). Neither absence announces
itself: the edge gap arrived as *"the filter is not visible"* on logbook, and the :8000 gap would arrive as
three unrelated tools quietly finding nothing. **After any Docker restart, check `docker ps -a` for Exited
containers before trusting a red** — `docker start <name>` is the whole fix, and it took four of them
(Docker Desktop → stack → edge runtime → api forwarder → Flask :5000) to get a truthful board.

**Named backlog — infra-health adoption is 7 of 92 (measured 2026-08-28).** `browser_gate_health.infra_exhausted`
exists and works (its self-test still proves the narrowness case: infra → SKIP, a real defect → still RED), but only
**7 of the 92 browser-driving validators import it**. The other 85 report a dead runner as a product defect, exactly
as dialog-floor did today. This is the §6m retry shape — the pattern is built, the adoption is the work — and it is
recorded as a number rather than averaged away. Wired today where the evidence pointed: `dialog-floor` plus the three
journey gates on the standing FAIL list (`join-lands`, `g5d-reauth-restore`, `timed-journey-family`), each of which
also now surfaces the prover's FULL output instead of its last three lines, since a truncated tail can hide the very
signature that classifies the failure. NOT blanket-patched: 85 mechanical edits nobody re-runs is how a false green
gets manufactured.

**Instrument lesson, stated once:** a failure-injection gate makes TWO claims — *the failure was induced* and
*the page answered correctly*. Only the second is about the product, and checking them in that order is what
keeps a harness breakage from becoming a false accusation. Three of this session's five reds were the gate.

## Synthesis (T1+T2) — fusion verdicts, not just findings

1. **STRONGEST FUSION: the platform has THREE auth-wall idioms — fuse toward ONE.**
   (a) `whSignInWall()` (new, 38 sites + idle path: redirect + `?return=`), (b) marketplace's
   `wh_return_to` sessionStorage + `setTimeout` redirect (predates T1; the `/workhive/`-scoped
   regex), (c) `whAuthRequiredToast` (in-place refusal with doors, for actions that should NOT
   navigate). Verdict: (a) and (c) are the two legitimate shapes — (a) when the whole PAGE is
   gated, (c) when one ACTION is gated on a browsable page. (b) is (a) wearing sessionStorage;
   marketplace's requirePostAccount should migrate to `whSignInWall()` in T5, deleting the
   bespoke regex (one return contract, one validator, currently two). Owner: utils.js. Blast
   radius: marketplace.html only.
2. **The conversion contract is now ONE function** (`whPrimaryCta`) with a mode switch —
   keep it that way: any future CTA variant (a campaign button, a pricing page) must route
   through it or the attribution + waitlist-revisit switch silently fork. The `cv_public_surface`
   lint enforces the doors; it cannot see a NEW bespoke JS opener — clickAudit's consequence
   probe is the live backstop.
3. **Instrument monoculture was the deep root**: every CTA oracle asserted existence because
   they all descended from the same static-scan idiom. The CV family deliberately mixes
   modalities (static lint + live click + journey + DB verification) — keep new trajectory
   locks modality-diverse; a wave whose locks are all static is re-growing the blind spot.
4. **Public templates are now first-class product surfaces** (roster, gates, gauntlets). The
   remaining second-class citizens: the hidden-nav pages (audit-log, ai-quality,
   ph-intelligence, founder-console, status) — T63-T78's exact mandate. No action now; named
   so the asymmetry is visible.
5. **Keep distinct (argued):** `whAuthRequiredToast` vs `whReadError` — both are refusal
   surfaces, but one refuses an ACTION to an anon (remedy = auth doors) and the other reports
   a failed READ to anyone (remedy = retry/status). Fusing them would blur the two truth
   conditions (the two-notices lesson).
