## Context

Ian (2026-08-23): *"diverse scenarios test will lead to its improvement of its full stack
architectural layers and system design for every production pages. we need to extend and expand
what we have."* His concrete pain: on his phone, the landing page's "Get early access for free"
sticky CTA is effectively dead; primary CTAs should just BE the signup; every sign-in surface
must offer sign-up. And his direction on scope (extended twice): *"think of this a trajectory 1
… do it comprehensively per trajectories … extend it up to diverse 200 trajectories"* — the
landing-conversion arc is ONE instance of a repeatable method, mirrored 200 ways across every
production page, persona, device, entry path, condition, and lifecycle stage.

Why this program exists: a 790-gate green board coexisted with a dead CTA on the most important
page. Exploration proved the mechanism — every CTA oracle on the platform is an *existence*
check, `#anchor` links are a universal regex blind spot, `[inert]` elements are exempted by
design, **the anonymous visitor is exempted from every journey verdict**, and the 109
learn/tools pages (the entire top-of-funnel) are in no UX denominator. Walking as a real user is
the only lens that sees this class — so it becomes the program.

## The Trajectory Method (codified from how T1 was derived — every trajectory mirrors it)

Each trajectory is one named user story: **persona × device × entry path × intent**, walked
live, driving fixes through every stack layer, then locked so the class can never silently
return.

1. **SPEC** — the story, its scenario-matrix cells, the pages/layers it crosses, its
   done-definition. Registered in `trajectory_registry.json` before any walk.
2. **WALK** — live MCP/Playwright walk AS that user (390 and/or 1280, correct auth state,
   correct entry). Every pain point recorded with file:line receipts (A7 discipline). A pain
   point = anything a real user would feel: dead/misleading affordance, wrong copy, lost work,
   silent failure, missing path, confusion.
3. **ROOT-CAUSE** — each pain traced through the stack (copy → DOM/CSS → JS handler → utils →
   edge/DB → architecture), and separately: *which instrument blind spot let it survive*.
4. **FIX** — product fixes, central-first (utils.js helpers before per-page edits; template
   fixes for template families), batched per A15 one-way-green.
5. **CLOSE THE INSTRUMENT** — the blind spot that hid each pain becomes a detector upgrade or a
   new prover/journey/dim (per DIMENSION_EXPANSION_FLYWHEEL: dims discovered by the walk, never
   invented; §12 no-redundancy proof before a new class id).
6. **LOCK** — bank rows + gates (`<family>_<oracle>` in run_platform_checks Platform group),
   with a **resurrection proof**: the new detector must go RED against the pre-fix world
   (git checkout / `_fixtures/`) and green on HEAD. "Calibrate the instrument, not the page."
7. **TEACH** — skills writeback + Memento; registry status advances spec'd → walked → fixed →
   locked.

Instruments accumulate: later trajectories get cheaper because earlier ones built the harnesses
(view_pass, dialog_targets, the CTA-activation prover, the anon journey class…).

## Trajectory 1 (fully specced): "Anon phone visitor converts from the landing page"

Ground truth from exploration (receipts in section below). Execution phases:

**T1.0 Product fixes** (fix-before-bank, one batched pass per shared file):
- `utils.js`: add `whPrimaryCta(source)` (conversion-mode switch, default `'direct'` → opens the
  real signup modal) and `whAuthRequiredToast(action, {allowSignup, returnTo})` (a refusal toast
  whose remedy is CLICKABLE: Sign in / Create account with `?return=`).
- `index.html` one pass: sticky CTA becomes a button → `whPrimaryCta('sticky')` (kills the
  dead-anchor + inert + no-smooth-scroll + no-suppression stack at :2695-2698/:3778-3790);
  hero :1345 + nav :1040/:1080 → `whPrimaryCta(...)`; add `?signup=1` to the deep-link resolver
  beside `?signin=1` (:3633); sign-in panel gains inline "Don't have an account? **Create one —
  free**" and signup gains the reciprocal (Ian verbatim); masthead: one Sign In + one primary
  Sign Up (not 3× Sign In); `#join` waitlist DEMOTED to an honest secondary "Get updates by
  email" block (default; retiring it entirely stays a one-edit revisit); `_supabaseSignup`
  gains `source` per entry point (attribution becomes measurable); remove the decorative role
  `<select>`; delete orphaned `#panel-guest`/`submitGuest`; FAQ :1994 + JSON-LD :250 rewritten
  from the provisioning-waitlist story to instant signup.
- Satellites: `public-feed.html` :147/:157 bare `index.html` → `?signin=1&return=` + a signup
  affordance on the primary CTA; `marketplace.html` gains the standard signed-out masthead and
  its 8 dead "Sign in to …" toasts (:1608…:4165) become `whAuthRequiredToast`;
  `engineering-design.js:32040` bare redirect → `?signin=1&return=` (the one outlier).
- Template families via a one-shot batch rewriter (`tools/retarget_public_ctas.py`): ~49 learn
  pages (nav gains Sign In; "Join the Hive"→ real signup deep link; "takes 30 seconds" claims
  become true) and ~60 tools pages (fix the false "no sign-up needed" claim that links into a
  gated page).
- Root hygiene: move `index-*-test.html` / `*.backup*.html` out of the served root into
  `_fixtures/` — kept deliberately as NEGATIVE FIXTURES for detector calibration.

**T1.1 Instrument fixes** (each named blind spot closed):
- `validate_link_target_existence.py`: stop excluding `#anchors`; add id-existence cross-check;
  roster derived, not hardcoded (its current roster scans 2 nonexistent pages silently and
  misses 17 real ones).
- `ufai_battery.js`: wire `clickAudit()` into the automated path (the only behavioral dead-CTA
  rule is currently dead code); widen `deadHref` beyond bare `#`; replace the `[inert]`
  exemption with a `cta:inert-primary` report; detect `addEventListener` bindings via an
  init-script wrapper so `deadFn` stops being inline-onclick-only.
- `prove_journey.mjs`: scope the 5 anon exemptions to signed-in oracles only; J3's `^#`
  exclusion becomes anchor RESOLUTION (id exists + click yields scroll/modal).
- `live_page_journeys.registry.mjs`: fix LA2's swallowed CTA click; add `signUp(ctx)` helper.
- Fix `ufai-rubric-spec.json` `_meta` drift (21/78 → 32/99) + re-run parity gates.

**T1.2 New scenario classes:** `substrate/reference/scenario_matrix.json` (72 cells: device ×
auth × entry × intent, with declared_na discipline) + `tools/validate_scenario_matrix.py`;
**J6 anon conversion funnel** in prove_journey (cold start, CTA → signup → account verified via
the existing psql `adminQuery`, disposable account cleaned); LA7-LA10 journeys (sticky-CTA
activation, sign-in-wall reciprocity, `?signup=1` deep link, marketplace toast remedy);
**`tools/prove_cta_activation.mjs`** — click every visible primary CTA (anon, both viewports),
assert an observable consequence (modal|navigation|scroll-delta|focus); new rubric class **CV
"conversion visibility"** with its §12 no-redundancy proof (not TR/X1/DP/L2/H1 — argued from
their recorded scopes).

**T1.3 Public-surface coverage** (the 109-page hole): `public_surface_registry.json`
(generated); template-deep (2 exemplars get the full prover) + instance-cheap
(`tools/public_surface_gate.py` static lint of all 109: nav resolution, CTA-href policy,
sign-in link present, claim-honesty lint banning "no sign-up needed"-class lies) + a rotating
5-page live sample per run.

**T1.4 Lock:** `banks/conversion_funnel_bank.json` OUTSIDE the fixed 200-row page banks (the
marketplace-877 precedent — cross-page subject, different denominator), rows keyed by
scenario-matrix cell, new oracle keys (`cta_activation`, `signup_affordance`, `signup_deeplink`,
`funnel_complete`, `claim_honesty`) added to the ONE vocabulary in
`build_live_mcp_registry.py`; gates `cv_funnel`, `cv_public_surface`, `link_anchor`,
`deploy_root_hygiene`, `roster_parity`; roster unification via
`substrate/reference/page_roster.json` + `tools/validate_roster_parity.py` (each consumer
declares its scope predicate so differing counts are explained, not drifted).

**T1.5 Verify:** resurrection tests per blind spot (red on pre-fix checkout/_fixtures, green on
HEAD); full board re-run including the new gates; and **the Ian test** — a scripted 390 anon
walk reproducing his exact phone session with screenshots: land → scroll → tap sticky CTA →
signup opens → account created → first value.

## The Trajectory Catalog (T2–T200) — full specs, each mirroring T1's method

Every trajectory below is specced with the same skeleton T1 used: **Story · Route · Layers ·
Known receipts** (facts already established with file:line, so the walk starts grounded) ·
**Pain probes** (the diverse-scenario questions the walk must ask) · **Fix targets** ·
**Instrument close** (the blind spot each pain class maps to) · **Lock + done**. The WALK still
decides the true pain list — the probes are the checklist, never the conclusion (A7: observed,
not assumed). Waves end with a mega-cycle + full board re-run.

---

### Wave A — Acquisition & first value (T1–T8)

### T2 — Anon lands on a learn article from search → reads → converts
- **Story**: anon, phone 390 (search traffic is mobile-heavy), entry = direct URL to a
  `/learn/<slug>/` article (organic search), intent = learn then convert.
- **Route**: learn article → in-body links → nav CTA → index auth modal → signup → first value.
- **Layers**: static template HTML → nav/CTA policy → index deep-link resolver → auth → DB.
- **Known receipts**: learn nav = Home/Learn/"Join the Hive"→`/#join` (waitlist), NO Sign In
  link on any of ~49 guides; "Join WorkHive first (free, takes 30 seconds)" → waitlist (false
  claim); in-body CTAs link into gated app pages that bounce to `?signin=1`;
  `tools/cta_gate.py` covers only in-body CTA presence.
- **Pain probes**: does every in-article link resolve (anchors included)? does the reading
  experience at 390 survive (Z2 reflow, T-class)? does a reader who wants the product see a
  truthful next step ABOVE the fold and at article end? does the gated-page bounce preserve
  intent (return-to after signup — not just signin)? do the article's claims about the product
  (counts, "free", "30 seconds") match reality (claim-honesty)? footer/related-article links?
- **Fix targets**: the learn template (via `tools/retarget_public_ctas.py` from T1.0 — T2
  verifies and extends it), index deep-link resolver `?return=` handling for signup.
- **Instrument close**: `public_surface_gate.py` (T1.3) gains the learn-template checks T2's
  walk finds missing; `prove_public_surface.mjs` exemplar = one learn article; the
  `from-learn` scenario-matrix column moves to covered.
- **Lock + done**: `cv_public_surface` covers learn instances; J6 variant `anon-from-learn`
  green; done = a phone reader can go article → signup → signed-in value with intent preserved,
  proven by the scripted walk + screenshots.

### T3 — Anon lands on a tools calculator from search → uses it → converts
- **Story**: anon, phone 390 + PC 1280 (engineers calc at desks too), entry = direct URL to a
  `/tools/<slug>/` calculator, intent = solve a problem now, convert if value shown.
- **Route**: calculator page → use the embedded calc → "full suite" CTA → engineering-design →
  auth wall → signup → land back in the design suite.
- **Layers**: static template → embedded calc JS → gated-page redirect →
  `engineering-design.js` identity gate → auth → return-to.
- **Known receipts**: "free, no sign-up needed for the calculators" links into
  `engineering-design.html` which REQUIRES identity; `engineering-design.js:32040` silently
  redirects to bare `index.html` (no modal, no message, no `?signin=1`) — the doubly-false
  claim; ~60 instances share one template.
- **Pain probes**: does the on-page calculator actually work standalone at 390 (inputs, keyboard
  type, results)? is the free-vs-gated boundary stated truthfully at the moment of the click?
  after signup, does the user land in engineering-design (return-to) or get dumped on the
  dashboard? do calculator results survive the auth round-trip (X2 interruption resilience —
  worth probing: a computed result lost at the wall is abandoned work)? unit/standard citations
  visible (domain-truth on public surface)?
- **Fix targets**: tools template (claim copy + CTA policy), `engineering-design.js` gate
  (message + `?signin=1&return=`), possibly a result-handoff (stash calc inputs in
  localStorage pre-redirect, restore after auth — reuse `whAutoSaveDraft` pattern).
- **Instrument close**: claim-honesty lint (T1.3) proves it catches this exact lie class
  (resurrection: red on the pre-fix template); `anon-from-tools` J6 variant added; Z1
  input-efficiency lens pointed at the embedded calculators (public pages never had it).
- **Lock + done**: `cv_public_surface` instance-lint green over ~60 tools pages; done = a
  calculator user converts without losing their computation, claims on the page are true.

### T4 — Anon browses public-feed → wants to reply/post → wall → converts
- **Story**: anon, phone 390, entry = shared link to public-feed (a worker shared a post),
  intent = join the conversation.
- **Route**: public-feed → read posts → tap reply/post → wall → signup → back to the SAME
  post with composer ready.
- **Layers**: public read RLS → feed render → auth wall UX → return-to with deep-link
  (post id) → community membership gate (a fresh account has no hive — what happens?).
- **Known receipts**: `public-feed.html:147,157` — "Sign In →" and the page's primary CTA
  "Sign in to post →" are bare `href="index.html"`: the modal never opens; no signup
  affordance anywhere; public-feed is the designated anon surface (its P1 persona is anon in
  the anatomy); posts deep-link via `?post=` (community's history-state pattern).
- **Pain probes**: after signup, the new user has NO hive — does the "reply" intent survive
  (community requires hive membership; the identity-seeding memory: session alone bounces
  community to the hive picker)? is that bounce explained or a dead end? does return-to carry
  the post id? can an anon reader even TELL which content is public vs hive-only (the
  visibility vocabulary)? share/copy-link affordances for anon?
- **Fix targets**: `public-feed.html` CTA hrefs (T1.0 does the mechanical fix; T4 walks the
  full intent-preservation chain), community's no-hive arrival state (honest "join or create a
  hive to reply" with the T6/T7 paths offered).
- **Instrument close**: J6 variant `anon-from-public-feed`; a new pain probe class for the
  scenario matrix: **intent preservation across the wall** (return-to + context) — extends JA2
  (return-promise kept) to the anon→signup crossing; LA10 (toast remedy) generalized.
- **Lock + done**: the `?return=` contract gated (an oracle asserting arrival lands on the
  promised subject); done = anon reader converts and lands back at the post with a truthful
  next step, even with zero hives.

### T5 — Anon browses marketplace signed-out → gated action → converts
- **Story**: anon, PC 1280 + phone 390, entry = direct marketplace URL (word of mouth: "you
  can buy parts there"), intent = browse listings, then save/watch/inquire.
- **Route**: marketplace browse → filter/search → open a listing → gated action (watchlist,
  inquiry, hail) → wall → signup → action completes.
- **Layers**: anon RLS read surface (public listings) → gated-action UX → auth → the 877-row
  marketplace registry's anon rows → credit economy visibility.
- **Known receipts**: marketplace signed-out has NO header/nav/auth control at all
  (:592-646); 8 "Sign in to …" toasts with no clickable remedy (:1608, :1828, :1886, :2153,
  :3389, :3806, :4112, :4165); `wh_return_to` sessionStorage exists (:3097-3099); MK1 anon
  browse journey exists (K6).
- **Pain probes**: can an anon visitor understand what the marketplace IS (value prop, trust
  signals TR-class) without an account? does every gated tap name the remedy AND offer it
  (whAuthRequiredToast from T1.0 — T5 verifies all 8 sites live)? does `wh_return_to` actually
  restore the interrupted action post-auth (or just the page)? listing deep-links shareable?
  price/credit vocabulary comprehensible pre-account?
- **Fix targets**: marketplace signed-out masthead (T1.0), the 8 toast call sites, the
  return-to action restoration (not just navigation).
- **Instrument close**: extend the marketplace registry's anon rows with `signup_affordance` +
  `cta_activation` oracles; LA10 marketplace variant becomes a K-series journey; the
  wall-crossing intent-preservation oracle from T4 reused.
- **Lock + done**: all 8 former toast sites gated green; done = anon → gated action → signup →
  the ACTION completes without re-finding the listing.

### T6 — Fresh signup → creates a hive → invites a teammate
- **Story**: new supervisor-to-be, PC 1280 (setup is a desk task), entry = post-signup landing,
  intent = set up the team's workspace.
- **Route**: first signed-in landing → hive.html onboard → Create a Hive → name it → invite
  code shown → share paths → (teammate joins in T7) → roster shows the join.
- **Layers**: onboarding UX → hive creation write (hives + hive_members) → invite-code
  generation (genCode) → share affordances → realtime roster update.
- **Known receipts**: walked LIVE on prod this week (smoke): btn-go-create → #hive-name-input →
  btn-submit-create → "HIVE CREATED … Share this code: HJJF2T" — the mechanics work; the
  createHive double-submit guard exists (hive.html "if (btn.disabled) return"); recoverHive
  membership branch + whReadError now on the failure path.
- **Pain probes**: is the FIRST signed-in screen a guide or a wall of empty tiles (O1
  value-first onboarding — the fresh-account ops-home showed "ALL CLEAR" + empty glance in the
  smoke; honest but is it HELPFUL)? does the invite code offer real share affordances on the
  spot (copy button, share sheet on phone, QR?) or just text to read aloud? what does the
  supervisor see while waiting (empty roster honesty)? can the code be retrieved LATER (where
  does it live after this screen)? is next-step guidance present (register assets, first PM)?
- **Fix targets**: hive.html post-create screen (share affordances, next steps), possibly
  index ops-home first-run state (a "set up your hive" path when tiles are empty).
- **Instrument close**: a J6 continuation journey `signup→hive→invite` (the K-series shape);
  first-run-guidance probes added to the O-class lens scope for the post-create screen.
- **Lock + done**: journey green incl. code retrievability; done = a new supervisor reaches
  "my teammate can join" without leaving the happy path or memorizing anything.

### T7 — Invited worker joins via code on phone
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, entry = index.html told "join with code HJJF2T" at briefing,
  intent = get into the team hive fast.
- **Route**: signup (or existing account) → hive.html → Join with Code → enter code → "YOU'RE
  IN" → first useful screen.
- **Layers**: join RPC + membership write → code validation UX → post-join landing → what the
  worker sees of the team's data immediately.
- **Known receipts**: walked LIVE on prod (smoke worker): btn-go-join → #join-code-input →
  submit → "YOU'RE IN … Your records are now visible to your team". Case sensitivity,
  whitespace, wrong-code refusal NOT yet probed. Community requires wh_active_hive_id seeding
  (the identity memory).
- **Pain probes**: wrong/expired code refusal — does it name the problem (why_refused)?
  code entry ergonomics at 390 (uppercase keyboard, paste support, 6-char format hint)?
  post-join: does the worker land on something USEFUL (the team's board) or an empty personal
  view? does "your records are now visible" explain what that MEANS (privacy comprehension)?
  double-join idempotency? kicked-then-rejoin path?
- **Fix targets**: hive.html join form (input ergonomics, refusal copy), post-join landing.
- **Instrument close**: join-code refusal cases join the why_refused family; a two-context
  T6+T7 paired journey (supervisor sees the join land in realtime — reuses the two-context
  cross-tenant harness pattern from Arc J).
- **Lock + done**: paired journey green; done = briefing-room reality works: hear a code, be
  in the hive with the team's board visible, under a minute, one hand.

### T8 — Returning user, session expired mid-task → re-auth → work preserved
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, entry = PWA icon after days away (token expired), intent =
  continue yesterday's half-done task.
- **Route**: open app → expired-session detection → re-auth (`?signin=1&return=`) → land back →
  drafts/filters/context intact.
- **Layers**: session-timeout.js → auth redirect contract → whAutoSaveDraft/G5 memory →
  per-page restore paths.
- **Known receipts**: `session-timeout.js:52` SIGN_IN_URL = `index.html?signin=1` (no
  return-to today!); ~24 pages use the pattern; G5 filter persistence is at 100% (PDDA);
  X2 drafts exist via whAutoSaveDraft; the session-died family (co_session_died,
  dialog_session_died) covers refusal honesty but NOT the return trip.
- **Pain probes**: does re-auth return the user to the PAGE they were on (SIGN_IN_URL carries
  no return today — likely the top finding)? with the VIEW/tab/filter restored (G5d resume)?
  with the draft intact (X2b)? does the expired banner name what happened and what survived
  ("nothing you did was lost" — whReadError's vocabulary now exists for reads; writes?)?
  multi-tab expiry coherence?
- **Fix targets**: `session-timeout.js` (append `&return=<current page+params>`), index
  resolver honoring it post-auth, spot fixes where restore fails.
- **Instrument close**: a `return_promise_kept` oracle for the re-auth crossing (JA2 extended
  to expiry); the J2 repeat-visit journey gains an expired-session variant.
- **Lock + done**: gate asserting the session-timeout redirect carries+honors return; done =
  expiry costs one sign-in and zero context on every core page.

### Wave B — Core field work, phone-first (T9–T18)

### T9 — Worker logs a repair one-handed on phone, with photo
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, gloved/one-handed field reality, entry = PWA icon mid-shift,
  intent = record a repair NOW, fast, without losing it.
- **Route**: open logbook → new entry form → machine/category/description → attach photo →
  submit → entry visible in list + stat pills move.
- **Layers**: form UX (Z1 keyboards, K2 44px targets) → photo capture/upload (storage) →
  insert + RLS → PM mirror trigger → list re-render → XP award ledger.
- **Known receipts**: logbook's read-failed panel + Retry now honest (my sweep); the
  double-submit guard family covers the submit; photo size assert exists (Q0 gate); the
  voice photo-intent journey exists; whAutoSaveDraft on the form (X2); stat pills dash on
  failed reads (v234 bump).
- **Pain probes**: the WRITE path on a phone — field order sane for one thumb? machine picker
  searchable (X3) or a 200-option scroll? photo: camera-direct or gallery-only, upload
  progress visible (PP1), failure recoverable without retyping? time-to-logged (the whole
  point: seconds, not minutes)? does the landed entry SHOW immediately (did_it_land) with
  XP explained (T17 seam)? interrupted mid-form by a call — draft survives (X2a/b)?
- **Fix targets**: logbook form ergonomics per findings; photo path feedback.
- **Instrument close**: a timed-journey oracle (time-to-value budget per journey — new,
  generalizes PP to whole flows); photo-path failure injection added to the CC family scope.
- **Lock + done**: J-series `worker-logs-repair-phone` green with a stated time budget; done =
  one-handed logging incl. photo, interruption-proof, visibly landed.

### T10 — Worker completes an assigned PM task from the schedule
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, entry = pm-scheduler from nav (or T13's handover), intent =
  see today's PM, do it, mark complete with evidence.
- **Route**: pm-scheduler → today's list → task detail → complete (completion-sheet V2) →
  compliance/streak feedback → next task.
- **Known receipts**: completion-sheet is the V2 dialog (openSheet, whModalA11y registered);
  pm_completions + attribution psql recipes exist (completion_attributed,
  compliance_recomputes, deferred_not_completed, missed_pm_traceable); PM overdue tile
  denominator fixed (…067).
- **Pain probes**: can the worker tell WHICH PMs are theirs vs the team's (scope clarity)?
  overdue vs due-today visual triage at a glance (K-class)? completion evidence (readings,
  notes) ergonomic on phone? deferral honesty (deferred ≠ completed — the recipe exists;
  does the UI make the distinction as clear)? does compliance % visibly move after completion
  (effect_visible + T32 seam)? NA-marked assets excluded explicitly on the glass?
- **Fix targets**: pm-scheduler task list triage + completion sheet per findings.
- **Instrument close**: completion journey joins the timed-journey family; deferral-vs-complete
  vocabulary check joins one_vocabulary's scope.
- **Lock + done**: journey green; done = a worker clears their PM list on the phone and
  believes the compliance number that results.

### T11 — Worker issues a spare part against a job → ripple visible
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, entry = mid-repair from logbook (or inventory direct), intent =
  take a part from stores, have the system agree with the shelf.
- **Route**: inventory (or logbook part-consumption) → find part (search) → issue qty →
  stock decrements → low-stock threshold crossing → reorder suggestion (lead time …070) →
  supervisor's low-stock view ripple.
- **Known receipts**: parts_decrement_exact + movement_leaves_row + last_unit_race psql
  recipes; the Add-Part second-open crash FIXED (asset-linker); low-stock tile now counts
  truthfully (…066) and carries lead_time_days (…070); consumption_names_part recipe.
- **Pain probes**: part FINDING under time pressure (X3 search, barcode? naming variants)?
  qty entry keyboard (Z1 numeric)? the race on the last unit (recipe exists — does the UI
  refuse gracefully)? does the logbook entry link the consumption (consumers_reconcile)?
  cross-page ripple: does index/alert-hub low-stock reflect within the session (T30 seam)?
  units on quantities everywhere (units_visible — the "3 parts" lesson)?
- **Fix targets**: inventory search/issue flow per findings.
- **Instrument close**: a cross-page ripple oracle (write on page A visible on page B within
  one reload — extends cross_surface_agreement from read-parity to write-propagation).
- **Lock + done**: ripple oracle green for the stock chain; done = shelf and system agree, and
  the person who took the part can prove it in one place.

### T12 — Worker records a voice journal entry (mic + typed fallback + 429 reality)
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, noisy plant, entry = voice-journal from nav, intent = capture
  a thought hands-free; fall back to typing when the mic can't.
- **Route**: mic record → transcribe → agent reply → entry saved; OR typed → send → saved.
- **Known receipts (incl. a LIVE finding to resolve)**: the typed send is COUPLED to the AI
  reply — `POST ai-gateway 429` = the entry row is never written (server-side write inside
  voice-journal-agent); the page IS honest ("your note was not saved", draft kept, whAiError
  toast) but the DESIGN loses the note when quota is drained. Transcribe path: voice-transcribe
  fn, low-confidence clarify branch; whReadError now on loadHistory; journal_private +
  attributed_from_jwt + pii_rule_holds + raw_survives_polish psql recipes.
- **Pain probes**: the architecture question first — should the note PERSIST first with the
  reply as enhancement (reply column is nullable — schema supports decoupling)? mic
  permission-denied path honest? transcription wait feedback (PP1/PP2 with cancel)? Filipino
  speech (T45 seam)? replay/listen affordance? history search at 390?
- **Fix targets**: the save-before-reply decoupling in voice-journal-agent + voice-journal.html
  (an edge-fn change — batched into a wave deploy); mic-path feedback per findings.
- **Instrument close**: a `work_survives_quota` oracle (user data must never be lost to an AI
  refusal — generalizes to every AI-coupled write surface, feeds T39).
- **Lock + done**: 429-with-note-preserved proven live (resurrection: red on the coupled
  design); done = no spoken/typed note is ever lost to quota, mic or not.

### T13 — Worker reads shift handover at shift start
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, clock-in moment, entry = dayplanner (or hive handover panel),
  intent = "what happened, what's mine, what's dangerous" in two minutes.
- **Known receipts**: dayplanner offline-copy honesty done (stale-labeled cards, UNKNOWN

- **Pain probes**: is there ONE canonical "start of shift" surface or three competing ones
  (dayplanner vs shift-brain vs hive handover — the fusion question, synthesis discipline)?
  carry-forward items visible with age? safety-critical items ranked first (K1)? does the
  2-minute read actually fit 390 without archaeology (A-class)? handover author attribution?
- **Fix targets**: per findings — possibly a synthesis verdict (fuse or clearly role the three
  surfaces).
- **Instrument close**: the timed-journey oracle applied ("2-minute handover" budget);
  cross-surface_agreement between the three handover-ish surfaces.
- **Lock + done**: one authoritative morning read, timed, with the other surfaces either
  fused or explicitly scoped; journey green.

### T14 — Worker goes offline mid-entry → queued write → reconnect sync
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, dead zone in the plant, entry = mid-T9 logbook entry, intent =
  finish the entry anyway and trust it syncs.
- **Known receipts**: THE FRAME HOLE — 8 pages register offline write queues (logbook IndexedDB

- **Pain probes**: mid-flight offline transition (not just offline-at-load): does the queue

  reconnect: auto-sync with receipt, or silent? conflict on sync (the entry's machine got
  renamed meanwhile)? photo in the queue? queue survives app restart (PWA)?
- **Fix targets**: per findings across the 8 queue pages.
- **Instrument close**: **the `offline_queued` oracle built** (replacing offline_refusal on
  queue pages via the in-frame displacement mechanism) + a reconnect-sync journey with
  network-flap injection (view_pass + context.setOffline choreography).
- **Lock + done**: the frame hole closed for all 8 pages; done = a dead-zone entry lands
  eventually with the worker never wondering whether it did.

### T15 — Worker searches fault history before a repair
- **Story**: worker, phone 390, about-to-open a machine, entry = logbook search (or asset-hub

- **Known receipts**: logbook search/team mode (renderEntries), asset-hub per-asset history,

- **Pain probes**: search findability from the repair context (is history one tap from the

## Verification (per trajectory and per wave)

1. **Resurrection proof per closed blind spot**: the new/upgraded detector runs red against the

   device/auth/entry, screenshots attached — T1's is Ian's literal phone session.
3. **Wave close**: mega-cycle (provers re-run, restamps, converter), full

   board may only be called green when the gates that would have caught each wave's pains are

## Execution order

T1 phases 0→5 first (it builds the harnesses every later trajectory reuses), then Wave A
(T2-T8, cheap — they reuse T1's instruments on adjacent funnels), then B→C→D (the core product
walked as its three user populations and their chains), then E (degraded sweeps — they need
B-D's journeys as their subjects), F, then G→H (persona + page-depth breadth), I→J→K (the
AI/economy/notification systems), L→M→N (context, scale, concurrency — heavy fixture reuse),
O→P→Q (arrival, compliance, comprehension sweeps), and R→S last (lifecycle + game day — they
compose everything before them; T196 and T200 are the program's two capstones). Fixture
strategy: the seeded-scale hive (T61), the aged hive (T129), and the year-compression harness
(T196) are built once and reused across their waves. Within every trajectory: fix-before-bank,
shared-file edits batched (A15), retrieve-first, all work inline; every wave closes with a
mega-cycle + full board + skills writeback + Memento handoff, and deploys land per completed
wave at Ian's standing gate.

## CD-invariant conversion pass — findings (2026-08-31)

Converting `live-walk` bank rows into permanent psql recipes is not bookkeeping: writing a probe forces
someone to state the invariant precisely and then prove it against the database, and three rows did not
survive that. Bank state moved 74 → 96 psql-backed rows (22 conversions), 839 → 817 live-walk.

### ★DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED — an anonymous visitor could read every public post author's internal user id

`public-feed`'s oracle reads *"the author identity shown is the author's public identity — never their
internal name or hive."* The page honours it exactly: `public-feed.html:261` fetches
`id, author_name, content, category, created_at`. The **data layer did not**. `anon` held a table-wide
`SELECT` on `community_posts` (relacl `anon=arwdxtm`), and PostgREST executes as the `anon` role — so
any holder of the publishable key could request `auth_uid` directly. Measured before the fix: readable
on **15 of 15** public posts, exposing **7 distinct authors across 2 hives**. `auth_uid` is stable, so
the exposure is a *correlation key*, not one identifier.

**Why no walk could have caught it.** A live walk reads the rendered page, and the rendered page was
innocent. The leak sat on the API surface the page declines to use — visible only from the data layer,
which is precisely what the psql conversion looks at.

**Two failed attempts before the fix worked**, both now written into the migration so the next reader
does not repeat them:
1. `REVOKE SELECT (auth_uid) … FROM anon` ran clean and changed **nothing** — a column-level revoke is
   inert while a table-wide grant stands. The blanket grant must go first, then an explicit column
   allowlist (fail-closed: a column added later is not granted until someone decides it should be).
2. That alone then **took the public feed down entirely**. `v_community_posts_truth` is
   `security_invoker`, so the view's own SELECT list is privilege-checked — while it still named
   `p.auth_uid`, every anon read failed with `permission denied`, not a hidden field. The column had to
   leave the view too, which is safe: all seven call sites (community.html ×6, nav-hub.js,
   public-feed.html) name their columns and **none** selects `auth_uid`; the view has no dependents.

Fix: `supabase/migrations/20260831000001_anon_cannot_read_post_author_uid.sql` (applied locally).
Verified: feed 15 rows for anon · `auth_uid` refused 42501 on the table, 42703 on the view ·
community.html's two column lists still return 32 rows. Locked by
`tools/psql_probes/public-feed__public_identity_only.sql`, which asserts the fix AND that the feed
still works — a fix that secures a page by breaking it is not a fix.

**Writes were checked and are fine:** `anon` also holds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants here, but every
policy requires `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL` — measured, an anon UPDATE and DELETE each affect **0 rows**
and INSERT is refused 42501. RLS is doing that job correctly; the grants are inert.

**OPEN FOR IAN (design, not a defect):** the same oracle says "never their … hive", and `hive_id` +
`hive_name` remain anon-readable — `hive_id` cannot simply be revoked because the truth view LEFT JOINs
`hives` on it, so every anon read would fail. The real question is product-level: *should a public post
carry visible hive attribution?* If yes the oracle's wording should be corrected; if no this needs a
dedicated public view. Recorded, not decided.

### Two oracles that measurement did NOT support — deliberately NOT converted

Converting these would have banked a claim the database refutes, so they stay `live-walk` and are
flagged here instead:

- **`engineering-design/standard_versioned`** — *"the governing standard and its version are stored
  with the calc."* `engineering_calcs` has **no standard or version column**: 30 calcs, 0 with a
  `standard` key in `inputs`/`results`. The standard appears only as **prose inside `narrative`**
  (30/30 mention one). So the claim is half-met — a standard is recorded, its *version* is not, and
  nothing structured survives to tell a reader that a result predates a superseded revision. That is
  the exact risk the oracle exists to prevent.
- **`project-manager/co_terminal`** — *"an approved change order cannot be re-approved or edited —
  terminal state frozen."* The *edited* half is enforced, well:
  `guard_change_order_terms_immutable` freezes cost, schedule, scope, title and requester once raised.
  The *terminal* half is not: `wh_guard_supervisor_approval` decides **who** may move the status
  (supervisor-only), never that an approved order is final — approved → rejected is an ordinary
  reviewer transition. Whether that is a bug or correct behaviour (a supervisor reversing an approval
  with an audit trail is defensible) is a product question; either way the oracle overstates today.

### Also skipped, for stated reasons

- `community/reaction_count_distinct` — the unique index is on `(post_id, worker_name, emoji)`, and the
  population is n=1: any probe would pass vacuously.
- `achievements/xp_is_ledger_sum` — the award writes its ledger row inside
  `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL`, so 45/58 pairs disagree *by design*; the oracle asserts a
  conservation the code deliberately declines to guarantee.
- `pm-scheduler/overdue_from_due_date` — `pm_assets` carries only `last_anchor_date`; overdue is
  computed client-side from anchor + frequency, so there is no DB-side truth to assert.

### A vacuity trap the conversion caught, worth keeping

`community/no_orphan_replies` first read "find a post with replies, delete it, assert they vanish."
`community_replies` is **empty** (0 rows against 111 posts), so the fixture subquery returned NULL, the
DELETE matched nothing, and the assertion *"its replies are gone"* was satisfied by a delete that never
happened — a green proving nothing. The recipe now **builds its own post and three replies inside the
transaction** and asserts it created them before drawing any conclusion from their absence. Any
invariant whose fixture comes from ambient data can fail this way; self-grounded fixtures cannot.

### `inventory/reservations_released` — orphan holds exist; recorded, not converted

*"A staged reservation is released when its job closes or cancels — no orphan holds."* Measured:
`parts_staged_reservations` holds **4 rows, all open** (`consumed_at` and `released_at` both NULL), and
**every one has `recommendation_id = NULL`** — the recommendation that created them was deleted and the
FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so the hold outlived its job and lost even the pointer back to it. There is
no release trigger on the table.

Severity is contained and worth stating precisely: **nothing in the database consumes these holds** — no
view references the table, and no view subtracts `qty_reserved` — so available stock is not silently
reduced today. The defect is that the release path does not exist, not that stock is currently wrong.
The fix is a product decision (release on recommendation delete via the FK, or a reaper), so it is
recorded here rather than guessed at.

### ★INSTRUMENT CLOSED — the 99 psql recipes were never re-run, so every "lock" was write-only

Converting rows exposed a structural hole worth more than the conversions. 96 bank rows carry evidence
kind `psql` and each names its recipe in a `replay` line — and **nothing executed them**. They were
proven once at bank time and never again. The bank's freshness machinery expires a row when its
declared deps change, which is correct for a claim *about a file* and says nothing about an invariant
living in the *database*, where a migration, a policy edit or a dropped grant can falsify a recipe while
every file it depends on sits untouched.

That is not theoretical: `public-feed__public_identity_only.sql` above is a regression lock for a real
leak, and a lock nothing executes locks nothing.

**New gate:** `tools/validate_psql_probe_suite.py`, registered in `run_platform_checks.py` (Platform,
`severity: fail`). Runs all 99 recipes sequentially in ~25s — cheap enough for every board, so it is
deliberately **not** `skip_if_fast`. No residue by construction: every mutating recipe wraps its teeth
in BEGIN/ROLLBACK and most assert their own restoration.

**It failed 3 of 99 on its first full run — and all three were INSTRUMENT faults, not product
regressions.** Forcing that distinction is the point of the gate:

| recipe | what broke | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `assistant__feedback_attributable` | compared a before-count taken as **postgres** against an after-count taken as **authenticated**, whose SELECT policy shows only their own rows (postgres saw 1, the user saw 0) — a good insert read as a refusal | probe fixed: counts the INSERT with `RETURNING`, one visibility |
| `logbook__pm_mirror_idempotent` | assumed `completed_at + 1 day` was free; the fixture worker had completions on **consecutive days**, so the dedup index refused it exactly as designed | probe fixed: the free day is computed from that pair's latest completion |
| `registry__ghost_retired` | asserted `marketplace_orders` holds **zero rows** — a proxy for "inert to clients" that **our own seeder** falsified with 6 lifecycle rows | proxy leg removed; security legs kept; the drift recorded (below) rather than re-greened |

All three are the same family the memory bank already names: *the instrument was wrong more often than
the code*. Two of them would have read as product regressions to anyone trusting the red.

**Flake handling, stated because silence here is dangerous.** The recipes take row locks and several
`SET ROLE`, so 99 back-to-back reproduce this repo's known flake-under-load class —
`assistant__citations_resolve_lawfully` failed inside the suite once, then passed three times standalone
and on every full run since. A failing recipe is retried **exactly once** and a flake is **printed as a
flake**, never folded into the pass. A false RED sends someone hunting a defect that is not there, and
teaches the team to re-run reds until they go green — which is how a real failure eventually gets waved
through.

**OPEN FOR IAN (second item):** `registry/ghost_retired` claims the custodial order/escrow console is
retired. `marketplace-admin.html:1026` **UPDATEs** `marketplace_orders` on dispute resolution, and the
seeder now populates it, while `founder-console.html:1910` still records the premise that the tables
"have never held a row and NO client path can write one". No client can *create* an order, so the
relation is not live — but it is no longer untouched either. Is that lifecycle retired, half-built, or
being revived? The recipe's security assertions hold either way; the retirement *claim* needs a
decision.

### The remaining 66 CD-invariant rows, triaged — the standing conversion queue

Sized honestly rather than left as "~47 convertible". Every remaining `live-walk` CD-invariant row was
read and placed in one of four buckets, so the next session starts from a decision rather than a survey.

**NEXT: bucket 1 — DB-provable, no browser (≈10 rows, the immediate queue).** These are the next unit,
in this order, each following the pattern the 22 conversions established (control leg + teeth both

#### The fix was verified on the PAGE, not only in the database

A note against my own earlier claim of "verified": every check on the auth_uid fix was a SQL check, and
the change touched a view the most public page on the platform reads. Proving the query still returns 15
rows is not the same as proving the page still works — that is the whole-artifact discipline, and it
applies to a security fix as much as to a redesign.

So public-feed.html was loaded in a real browser at 390 as a genuinely ANONYMOUS visitor (no sign-in),
after the migration: **no console errors, no error state, no empty state**, and — the check that
actually matters — the newest public post's own content, pulled from the database and searched for in
the rendered text, **is present**, with author attribution showing. The signed-out conversion copy
("Sign In", "Sign in to post", "Create a free account") renders alongside it.

That closes the loop the SQL could not: the leak is shut AND the public window still works.

### NEXT ARC — `boundary_not_emptiness`: 34 rows, one oracle, and no gate covers it

The largest single cluster left in the banks is 34 `CH-ufai-I` rows that all carry the **same** oracle:
*"a permission boundary reads as 'not visible with this session', never as 'nothing here'."* One harness
could settle all 34, which makes it the highest-leverage remaining unit.

**No existing gate covers it, checked rather than assumed.** `empty-state-discrimination` is about
search-0 vs first-run empty; `failed-read-is-not-empty` is about a read that ERRORED rendering as
absence; `auth-boundary` is about enforcement (does the server refuse), not about the sentence the page
shows afterwards. This oracle is the third distinct thing: the read SUCCEEDED, the server lawfully
returned nothing, and the question is whether the page says *"you can't see this"* or *"there's nothing
here."*

**Why it is hard, and why it is probably unmet on most surfaces.** RLS refuses by FILTERING, not by
raising — a `USING` clause returns zero rows and no error. So a foreign-hive read and a genuinely empty
hive are byte-identical at the client unless the page makes a separate membership/role check and says so.
The platform's own strongest tool for refusing is therefore structurally invisible to the reader.
Same root as the logbook foreign-edit recipe converted this session, where a foreign UPDATE touches
0 rows and reports success.

**A crude static census** (`*.html`, permission/no-access vocabulary) found the word absent entirely from
~10 core surfaces — index, inventory, pm-scheduler, project-manager, dayplanner, skillmatrix,
achievements, engineering-design, public-feed, analytics-report — and thin (1–2 hits) on analytics,
alert-hub, asset-hub and shift-brain. **Treat that as a LEAD, not a finding:** the pattern also matches
unrelated uses (microphone permission), and absence of the word is not proof of absence of the state.
It says where to look, nothing more.

**The unit, when the walk lane is free:** sign in as a member of hive A, request an object belonging to
hive B (the deep-link path T43 already exercises), and record per surface whether the page distinguishes
refusal from emptiness. That produces the evidence 34 rows are waiting on, and — if the census is right —
a fix class worth more than the rows: *the platform's refusals are currently silent by construction.*

#### The lead was then checked precisely on four core pages — and it holds

The crude census above was treated as a lead, so four surfaces were opened and read rather than grepped:

- **pm-scheduler** carries THREE distinct absence states — `#no-results` ("No PM tasks match those
  filters", the search-0 case), `#dash-empty` (first-run), `#det-history-empty` ("No completions recorded
  yet") — and **no refusal state at all**.
- **inventory** appeared to have four refusal-vocabulary hits. Opened: every one is a source COMMENT or
  an unrelated toast ("Part removed from inventory."). **Zero** refusal states.
- **dayplanner**: one hit, same character. **achievements**: zero.

So the precise check did not soften the lead, it **hardened** it — and it also confirms the grep was
overcounting, which is why it was labelled a lead rather than a finding.

**The scenario that makes this bite is not exotic.** A worker removed from a hive keeps
`wh_active_hive_id` in localStorage. Their next read is lawfully refused by RLS — which FILTERS — so the
page receives zero rows and renders *"No completions recorded yet"*. The platform has already recorded
this exact shape once: a dead session's 0-rows-and-no-error was read as removal
(`a_dead_session_read_as_removal`). It is the same silence, arriving from the other direction, and it is
the T25 kicked-user experience seen from the data layer.

**This is now a specced arc, not a hunch:** the walk (member of hive A requesting hive B's object, and a
removed member re-opening the app) supplies the runtime half, and the fix class — a membership
discriminator the refusal path can speak from — is shared across every surface. 34 rows settle on it.

#### The census, run platform-wide: 25 of 26 surfaces cannot tell a refusal from an absence
> **⚠ SUPERSEDED — the real figure is 10 of 26. This section's number came from a broken instrument;
> see "The census was wrong by 2.5x" below. The reasoning here stands, the count does not.**

`tools/census_boundary_not_emptiness.py` (new — a census, deliberately not yet a gate) strips HTML and JS
comments first, because the crude pass counted four "refusal states" in inventory.html that were every
one a comment or an unrelated toast. Measured across 42 root surfaces:

> **26 own an absence state. ~~25~~ → **10** of those carry no refusal copy at all.** (superseded, below)

**The single exception is the reference implementation, and it is already in this repo.**
`marketplace.html:1222-1226` keeps three separate flags with the reasoning written beside them:
`_rateLimited` (a 429, with the human-readable wait), `_authExpired` (a 401 — "the remedy is signing in,
not retrying"), and `_accessDenied` — *"a 403 is a REFUSED ROW with a perfectly good session, and signing
in again cannot fix it — a different fact needing different words."* Line 2666 resets it per load, so a
since-granted permission does not keep reading as denied. So the fix class for the other 25 is
**propagate an idiom this codebase already wrote and reasoned about**, not invent one.

**★AND THE EXCEPTION ONLY COVERS THE LOUD HALF — which sharpens the whole arc.** `_accessDenied` fires on
a **403**: a grant or policy violation the server announces. The case that produced these 34 rows is the
**silent** one — RLS *filtering* a row out returns **200 with zero rows**. Even marketplace, the one
surface that distinguishes refusal from absence, cannot see that; nothing in an HTTP status tells it.
Distinguishing the silent refusal needs a separate membership/role read the page can speak from — which
is why the census also reports whether each surface has a discriminator at all, and why so many say NO.

**Limits of this instrument, stated so nobody over-reads it:** it proves the NECESSARY condition only. A
page with zero refusal states provably cannot distinguish; a page with them still has to be WALKED to
show the copy fires on the right branch. The discriminator heuristic is also incomplete — it looks for
membership/role reads and therefore scores marketplace as `NO`, because marketplace discriminates on an
HTTP status instead. That is a real limitation of the census, not a defect in marketplace.

#### Refining the census found the fix is cheaper than the count suggests

The first census printed one yes/no for "can this page ask whether it was refused?" and scored
**marketplace.html as NO** - the single surface that actually discriminates. An instrument that marks the
reference implementation as the worst case is measuring the wrong thing, so the column was split, because
the two ways of asking are genuinely not equivalent:

- **membership** - a hive_members / role / status read. The only way to catch the **silent** refusal,
  where RLS filters the row out and the response is an ordinary 200 with zero rows.
- **http-status** - a 403/401 branch. Catches only the **loud** refusal the server announces. This is
  what marketplace has, which is why its `_accessDenied` cannot see a filtered row either.

**The refinement changed the read of the backlog.** pm-scheduler and inventory each own FOUR absence
states, zero refusal copy - and both already carry **membership** machinery. They can already ask the
question; they simply never say the answer. The gap on those surfaces is a sentence and a branch, not new
plumbing - so the 25-surface backlog is mostly copy plus a branch on machinery that already exists, and
the expensive cases are the few with neither.

#### ★CORRECTION: the census said 25 and the number was 24 — my regex, not the product

The live walk caught the static census in the same mistake the census was built to catch. **shift-brain**
was scored as having *no refusal copy*. It answers a hiveless session with 245 characters:

> *"Shift Brain needs a hive. The autonomous shift planner runs hive-by-hive. Join or create a hive to
> see briefings for your team. **Go to Hive**"*

That names the boundary **and** offers the remedy — it is the behaviour the whole arc is asking for, and
my vocabulary simply did not contain the words the product used. A census whose vocabulary is narrower
than the product's is measuring its own wording, and it errs **pessimistically**: it invents a backlog
out of surfaces that were already handling the case.

Both instruments were widened (the census and the walk harness) and the baseline is **24, not 25**.
The baseline file says so in its own `_doc`, because the drop must not be read as progress:
**25 → 24 is an instrument correction; no page changed.** Recording it as a gain would have banked a fix
that never happened — the same error class as a proxy assertion quietly re-greened.

**A second instrument fix from the same run.** The walk reported `analytics.html` as *"REFUSAL NAMED"*
but stored only the first 260 characters of the page, which contained nothing of the sort — so the
verdict could be neither confirmed nor refuted without re-running the entire walk. The harness now
records the **matched phrase and 70 characters of context on either side** for both the absence and the
refusal branch. A verdict owes the reader the evidence that produced it.

### boundary_not_emptiness — the WALK, run as a removed member (2026-08-31)

`tools/walk_boundary_not_emptiness.mjs` signs in as a real user and points `wh_active_hive_id` at a hive
they do not belong to. Every hive-scoped read is then lawfully filtered to zero — the removed-member
state, reached **without mutating anyone's membership**. Premise verified first: only `hive.html` and
`index.html` ever write that key, and none of the 12 walked surfaces does, so the injected value holds.

**Result: 4 name the refusal, 4 answer with emptiness, 4 render neither.**

**The four that get it right — and analytics is the best implementation on the platform:**

> **analytics.html** — *"…your account does not have access to it. **Your session is fine.** Ask a
> supervisor if you need it."*

It names the boundary, explicitly separates it from a session problem (the confusion this whole class
produces), and gives the remedy. `asset-hub` and `shift-brain` answer *"needs a hive"*; `project-manager`
*"Join or create a hive"*. Better than marketplace's `_accessDenied`, which only catches a loud 403 —
these speak to the person.

**The four that answer with emptiness, worst first:**

| surface | what a removed worker is told |
|---|---|
| **alert-hub** | **"All clear — No critical alerts, anomalies, or pending briefs for your hive right now."** |
| community | "No activity yet." |
| pm-scheduler | "Nothing due in the next 14 days" |
| dayplanner | "EMPTY" |

**★alert-hub is not a UX wrinkle — it is a false safety assurance.** *"All clear"* is an affirmative
claim about a plant the platform cannot see a single row of. This repo already fixed the sibling class
for reads that ERROR ("a read that FAILED must not render as 'there is nothing'"); the REFUSED read
slipped through the same gap, and on the one surface where the sentence is a safety statement.

**★pm-scheduler makes the fix cost obvious — it ALREADY KNOWS.** `validateHiveMembership()`
(pm-scheduler.html:1213-1232) queries `hive_members` and, on `!membership || status === 'kicked'`, logs
`console.warn('worker is no longer an active hive member')`, clears four localStorage keys, sets
`HIVE_ID = null` and returns. **The page computes the exact fact the user needs and puts it in the
console.** This is precisely what the static census predicted for it — *membership discriminator: yes,
refusal copy: none* — so static and runtime agree, and the fix is a sentence on a branch that already
exists, not new plumbing.

**Not a defect, stated so nobody "fixes" it:** dayplanner's numbers stay populated because
`schedule_items` is **per-person** (keyed by `auth_uid`, as its own tenant-isolation recipe records) —
a worker's own plan is correctly theirs regardless of hive. Its "EMPTY" pill is about a day with no
items, not about a boundary.

**NEXT on this arc:** the 4 "neither" surfaces (inventory, logbook, achievements, skillmatrix) need
their rendered state read — they matched neither vocabulary, which may mean a third state (a stuck
skeleton, a redirect) rather than good behaviour. Then the fix batch, cheapest first: pm-scheduler's
existing branch, then alert-hub's "All clear" guard, using analytics' sentence as the model.

#### The census overstated readiness too — and it did so exactly where the cost is

"Has a discriminator" was one column, and it lumped a real membership **query** together with mere role
**vocabulary**. That credited `alert-hub` and `community` with the ability to tell a refusal from an
absence, while `alert-hub` contains **no `hive_members` read at all** — only `HIVE_ROLE` strings, which
say what a member may *do*, not whether this person still *is* one. Different jobs, different cost, and
the column was hiding the difference on the surface that needs the fix most.

Split three ways, ordered by how close a page already is to being able to say it:

| discriminator | surfaces (of the silent ones) | what the fix costs |
|---|---|---|
| **membership-query** | pm-scheduler, inventory, community | the page already asks the server — **say the answer**. pm-scheduler literally `console.warn`s it. |
| **http-status** | marketplace | catches the loud 403; blind to the silent filtered read |
| **role-vocab-only** | **alert-hub** | the check must be **added** before anything can be said |

**So the one surface saying "All clear" to a person who can see nothing is also the one that cannot
currently tell.** That is the arc's priority ordering, produced by the instrument rather than by taste:
pm-scheduler is a sentence on a branch that already exists; alert-hub needs the branch first, and it is
the one where the wrong answer is a safety claim.

#### alert-hub has already been bitten by this exact sentence once

The fix for `alert-hub` does not need arguing from principle — the page argues it in its own source.
`alert-hub.html:568-572` carries this comment:

> *"canonical anomaly count held in module state … so the Plain-Read summary reads it directly instead of
> DOM-scraping the rendered badge (which raced: the fire-and-forget `loadAnomalyEngine` could leave the
> verdict reading **"All clear"** for up to 60s while critical signals were still loading). Starts null =
> "not yet known"."*

Someone already found *"All clear"* rendering while the truth was unknown, diagnosed it, and fixed that
cause — even introducing `null` to mean **"not yet known"**, the exact distinction this arc is about.
The **refused** read is the same sentence and the same failure mode arriving by a different route, and
it was not covered.

The markup is static and unconditional (`alert-hub.html:402-406`): `#empty` holds a ✓ icon, *"All
clear"*, and *"No active alerts in your hive right now."* It has no state in which it can say *"we could
not read your hive."* So the fix is the branch alert-hub's own `_anomalyCount = null` convention already
models: **absence, refusal, and not-yet-known are three states, and only one of them is "All clear."**

### ★THE CENSUS WAS WRONG BY 2.5x — and the instrument failed in two independent ways

The headline above said **25 of 26 surfaces cannot tell a refusal from an absence.** The real figure is
**10 of 26.** Sixteen surfaces were already handling the case and were being counted as broken. No page
changed at any point; every movement in this number was my instrument.

**Cause 1 — the vocabulary was narrower than the product's, four separate times.** Each widening found
more surfaces that already worked: `needs a hive` (shift-brain); `Create or join a Hive` where the
pattern knew only *"join or create"* — the same sentence reversed (logbook, which also promises the
return trip); `does not have access` where it knew only *"do not"* (analytics). Enumerating phrasings
loses to the product every time.

**Cause 2 — and this one was invisible: literal BACKSPACE bytes in the pattern.** A Python edit wrote
`\bhive\b` intending word boundaries; what reached the file was `0x08` + `hive` + `0x08`. The clause
therefore required an actual backspace character in the page text and **could never match anything**.
It looked correct in every listing — `cat -v` and a `repr()` were what exposed it — and it silently
removed the single most productive alternative from both instruments. Same family as the null bytes
written into source earlier this session: an escape that survives review because it looks right.

**The count moved 25 → 24 → 22 → 10 with the product untouched.** Corrected in all three places it had
been recorded: this document, the `boundary-refusal-ratchet` gate label, and the T43 registry basis. The
baseline file's `_doc` now says a past decrease must be read as an instrument correction unless someone
confirms a page changed — because two of these decreases would otherwise read as fixes that never
happened.

**What survives unchanged, and it is the part that mattered:** `alert-hub` still answers a person who can
read nothing with **"All clear"**, and `pm-scheduler` still detects the removal in
`validateHiveMembership()` and tells only the console. Those were found by the WALK, against rendered
text, not by the regex census — which is precisely why the arc needed both instruments, and why the walk
is the one to trust when they disagree.

### ★THE CENSUS SWUNG 25 → 1; THE WALK NEVER MOVED. That is the finding about the instruments.

Final count on the static census: **1 of 26**, after crediting pages that route failures through the
shared error taxonomy. The full history, with the product untouched throughout:

| reading | what changed | product |
|---|---|---|
| 25 | first vocabulary | unchanged |
| 24 | learned "needs a hive" | unchanged |
| 22 | learned "Create or join" (word order) | unchanged |
| 10 | **literal backspace bytes** repaired; learned "does not have access" | unchanged |
| **1** | credited `whReadError`/`whListError` — copy that lives in **utils.js**, not the page | unchanged |

The last step is the one worth keeping. `analytics.html` was listed as having no refusal copy while the
walk watched it render *"your account does not have access to it. Your session is fine. Ask a supervisor
if you need it."* — because that sentence lives in `utils.js:937/:2354` and appears **zero times** in
analytics.html. **A per-file static census structurally cannot see centrally-provided copy, and grading
pages on literal strings punishes exactly the centralisation this platform built.**

**Meanwhile the walk gave the same answer three times running**, before and after every instrument
repair: **4 surfaces answer a removed member with emptiness — alert-hub *"All clear"*, community *"No
activity yet"*, pm-scheduler *"Nothing due"*, dayplanner *"EMPTY"*.** Five name the refusal (logbook,
asset-hub, analytics, project-manager, shift-brain); three render neither (inventory, achievements,
skillmatrix).

**So the census is demoted to what it can honestly support** — a floor check that a surface has *some*
way to say it — and the walk is the authority for whether it *does*. The ratchet stays (it would still
catch a page shipped with no route to refusal at all), with its baseline `_doc` recording that a past
decrease means an instrument correction, not a fix.

**The product finding is unchanged by any of this**, which is the point: `dayplanner`, `achievements`
and `skillmatrix` are per-person surfaces where a hive boundary does not apply, leaving **three real
defects — alert-hub, community, pm-scheduler** — and `inventory` to be read. alert-hub remains first:
it is the one whose empty state is a safety claim, and the one that must *add* the membership check
rather than merely say what it already knows.

#### The last "neither" resolved — and the silent FALLBACK is worse than the empty state

`inventory` matched neither vocabulary, and its own empty state ("No parts in inventory yet") *would*
have matched — so it was never shown. Captured directly under a foreign hive (`#empty-state` hidden,
`#no-results` hidden, 0 skeletons, list empty), the page renders:

> *"5 parts · 1 low · 0 out … PARTS AT HEALTHY STOCK 1 of 5 … 1 part at or below the reorder threshold.
> Order them before the next shift planning so they arrive before they hit zero. Longest lead time among
> them: 7 days."*

**Fully populated, confident, actionable data — while the hive context the user thought they were in has
silently evaporated.** Like pm-scheduler, inventory re-validates membership, finds none, clears the hive
keys and falls back to a personal/unscoped view. Neither says a word.

**This reframes the arc's severity ordering.** A blank "No entries yet" at least *looks* like nothing
happened. A **silent fallback** shows a plausible, well-formed dashboard for a *different scope* than the
user believes they are in — and gives them numbers to act on. "Order them before the next shift planning"
is advice about a shelf that may not be the shelf they are standing at.

**The corrected defect set — four hive-scoped surfaces, none of which tells a removed member anything:**

| surface | what happens | knows already? |
|---|---|---|
| **alert-hub** | says **"All clear"** — a safety claim | **no** — role vocabulary only, the check must be added |
| **inventory** | silent fallback to a populated personal view | yes — re-validates, then clears silently |
| **pm-scheduler** | silent fallback + "Nothing due"; `console.warn` only | yes — `validateHiveMembership()` |
| community | "No activity yet." | yes |

`dayplanner`, `achievements` and `skillmatrix` remain correct-by-design (per-person data). alert-hub is
still first — its wrong answer is a safety assurance — but inventory and pm-scheduler are now second and
third on *impact*, not just cost, because a confident wrong scope beats a blank one for causing harm.

#### The fix design — every piece already exists in this repo

Not a new pattern to invent. Three parts, each with a precedent in the codebase, batched into one edit
wave **after** the running board and its restamp complete (editing these files now would invalidate
in-flight gate reports and cost the re-earn).

**alert-hub — a third state, using its own established shape.** `alert-hub.html:512-514` already carries
the diagnosis for the sibling case: *"A FAILED READ IS INVISIBLE ON THIS PAGE TWICE OVER, which is why it
rendered 450 characters and said nothing under an injected 500"* — fixed with `Promise.allSettled` plus
`status === 'fulfilled'` checks. And `:568-572` introduced `_anomalyCount = null` meaning **"not yet
known"**, precisely so *"All clear"* could not render before the truth was in. The page therefore already
believes that **absence, failure and not-yet-known are different**. The refused read is the fourth state
it never got: a 200 with zero rows because RLS filtered them. It needs the membership check first — the
census scores it `role-vocab-only`, and there is no `hive_members` read in the file.

**pm-scheduler and inventory — say the thing you already computed.** Both call a membership
re-validation, find none, clear four localStorage keys and fall back to a personal view.
`pm-scheduler.html:1227` even writes the sentence — to `console.warn`:
*"worker is no longer an active hive member. Clearing hive state."* The user-facing half is missing. Reuse
`validateHiveMembership()` verbatim as the model; it is already correct, it simply has no voice.

**The copy already exists too.** `utils.js:2354` — *"You do not have access to `<thing>` with this
account. Your session is fine. Ask a supervisor if you need it."* — is exactly right, and is why
analytics passes the walk. Route the new branches through the shared taxonomy rather than writing four
new sentences; that is what made analytics correct without a word of its own copy, and it keeps the four
surfaces from drifting apart.

**Verification when the batch lands:** re-run `tools/walk_boundary_not_emptiness.mjs`. It has returned
the same four silent surfaces on three consecutive runs, so a change in that list is signal, not noise —
and the ratchet plus the walk together give the before/after that closes the 34 bank rows.

#### Reading the code changed the fix — the fallback is DELIBERATE; only the announcement is missing

`inventory.html:2445-2470` is worth quoting, because it turns this from "the page is broken" into
something narrower and fairer. `validateHiveMembership()` handles the removal explicitly:

```js
if (!membership || membership.status === 'kicked') {
  console.warn('Worker is no longer an active hive member. Clearing hive state.');
  [...4 keys].forEach(k => localStorage.removeItem(k));
  HIVE_ID = null; HIVE_ROLE = '';
  return true; // solo mode: inventory still usable for own items
}
```

**That is a considered design decision, and a defensible one** — a worker who loses their hive can still
track their own spares rather than being locked out. The defect is not the fallback. It is that the
transition is **unannounced**: the page changes the scope of everything on screen and says so only to the
console. So the fix is not "add a refusal state" but **"announce a degradation you already decided on"** —
smaller, and it does not argue with the original design.

Two details that make it cheaper still:
- **The function's return value is dead.** All three paths `return true` (DB error fails open, removal
  falls back, success), so the boolean carries no information and `inventory.html:2490` correctly
  discards it. Returning a discriminated result — or setting a `_hiveLost` flag beside the existing
  `_loadError`-style flags — is the whole plumbing change.
- **pm-scheduler's copy of the same function is void** and writes the same sentence to `console.warn`
  (`pm-scheduler.html:1227`). One shared helper would fix both and stop them drifting, which is the
  lesson the `_accessDenied`/`whReadError` centralisation already taught on this platform.

**So the batch shrinks to:** one shared "your hive context was lost" announcement routed through the
existing taxonomy, called from the two `validateHiveMembership()` copies; a membership check added to
alert-hub (which has none) so **"All clear"** can be suppressed when the platform cannot see the hive;
and community's empty state given the same branch.

### ★THE SYNTHESIS: this platform learned "failure ≠ emptiness" and never learned "refusal ≠ emptiness"

Every one of the four silent surfaces has **already been fixed for the sibling case**, and each says so
in its own source. That is the finding — not four unrelated bugs, one blind spot with a shape:

| surface | its own comment about the FAILED read | the REFUSED read |
|---|---|---|
| **alert-hub** | `:512` *"A FAILED READ IS INVISIBLE ON THIS PAGE TWICE OVER… it rendered 450 characters and said nothing under an injected 500"* — fixed with `allSettled` + status checks; `:568` even added `null` = "not yet known" so **"All clear"** could not render early | still renders **"All clear"** |
| **community** | `:1193` *"`error \|\| empty` COLLAPSED A FAILED READ INTO 'No activity yet.' … not a smaller claim than the truth, a different and discouraging one"* — error and empty now branch separately | the refused read still lands in the empty branch |
| **inventory** | `:2485` documents an auth-attachment race where *"the first initData reads can return empty (RLS rejected)"* — caught by a KPI parity sentinel | falls back to solo mode, unannounced |
| **pm-scheduler** | same `validateHiveMembership()` shape | `console.warn` only |

**Three states were learned; a fourth was never named.** The platform now distinguishes *the read
failed*, *the read is not back yet* (`null` = not yet known), and *there is genuinely nothing*. What no
surface models is **the read succeeded and the server lawfully returned nothing because you may not see
it** — because RLS refuses by FILTERING, so that case arrives as a perfectly ordinary `200` with zero
rows and is indistinguishable from an empty hive without a separate membership question.

**This is why the 34 bank rows all carry one oracle.** They are not 34 page bugs; they are one missing
concept, and the fix is one shared vocabulary — a fourth state beside the three each page already
models — applied at four call sites. It also explains why the static census was so unhelpful: the pages
*have* the words (they route through `whReadError`), they simply never reach that branch, because
nothing tells them this case exists.

**Precedent for the shape of the fix:** `marketplace.html:1222-1226` already keeps `_rateLimited`,
`_authExpired` and `_accessDenied` as three distinct facts with the reasoning written beside them. The
platform's own best implementation is a taxonomy of refusal states; the other surfaces need the same
distinction, sourced from `utils.js` so they cannot drift.

### THE FIX BATCH LANDED — the fourth state, named once and used five times

Applied after the board crashed and freed the edit window (see the `args` bug below). Two helpers in
`utils.js`, five call sites, no page inventing its own wording:

- **`whHiveContextLost(what)`** — the sentence, bilingual, beside `whReadError` because it is the same
  kind of fact. *"You are no longer a member of the X, so its data is not shown. **Your session is
  fine.** Showing only what belongs to you. Ask a supervisor to add you back if this is wrong."* The
  "your session is fine" half is load-bearing and copied deliberately from the 403 branch: the thing a
  person reaches for first is their own login, and re-authenticating cannot fix a membership change.
- **`whHiveMembershipLost(db, hiveId, workerName)`** — asks the question RLS answers silently, and
  **fails open**: a DB error returns `false`, because *"I could not ask"* is not *"you were removed"*, and
  an outage must not put a false accusation on screen.
- **`whHiveContextNotice(hiveName)`** — shows it in `_whShowNotice`, the region utils.js already reserves
  for standing facts. Explicitly not a toast: `utils.js:940` settled that argument for the sibling case —
  *"a toast that fades leaves the person looking at the same unexplained dashes, which is the whole
  defect."*

| surface | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **pm-scheduler** | "Nothing due in the next 14 days" | **VERIFIED** — names the refusal |
| **inventory** | silent fallback to a populated personal view | **VERIFIED** — names the refusal |
| **alert-hub** | **"All clear"** | third branch in `renderFeed`, ahead of the F40 filter case |
| **community** | "No activity yet." | leaderboard names the refusal |
| **dayplanner** | plant-PM rail returned `''` and vanished | rail says why it is empty |

**Each fix went where the page already had the machinery**, which is why the batch is small: alert-hub
already branched two ways on empty (F40: *"don't claim 'All clear' when a KIND filter is hiding
matches"*) and needed a third; dayplanner already had `plantWorkFailed` guarding the same rail under the
comment *"Silence is only honest when the read ANSWERED"* — it answered, it was refused; community had
already separated error from empty on this exact string. **Nothing here argues with an existing design.
pm-scheduler and inventory keep their solo-mode fallback; it is now announced rather than silent.**

`alert-hub`'s inline probe was refactored onto the shared helper immediately after writing it — a second
hand-rolled copy is precisely the drift `whReadError` was centralised to stop, and four copies is how
this platform's failure voice fragmented the first time.

### ★THE BOARD COULD NOT FINISH — one unguarded dict key, and every downstream re-earn refused

`run_platform_checks.py` crashed after **66 minutes** of successful gate runs:

```
KeyError: 'args'   at   cmd = [interp, v["script"]] + v["args"]
```

Nineteen registered gates carry only a `script` and a `label` — `selection-is-exposed`,
`shared-button-invites-the-click`, `the-return-promise-is-kept-safely` and sixteen more, all added in the
working tree, **none of them wrong**: a gate that takes no arguments has no reason to write `"args": []`.
The runner treated an optional key as required and died on the first one it reached.

**Why it stayed hidden, and why it cost the whole day's re-earn.** The crash lands at the END of a long
board, so it reads as a late-stage failure rather than a registration schema mismatch. And because the
run never closed, **`platform_health.json` was never written** — which is exactly why every restamp this
session refused: the gate *reports* were fresh on disk, but the run that would bless them never finished.
The restamp was correct to refuse; it was waiting on a file that was never going to arrive. I spent an
hour treating "the board is still running" as the blocker when the board had already been dying for
weeks' worth of runs.

Fixed at the runner, not by adding `"args": []` nineteen times:
`cmd = [interp, v["script"]] + list(v.get("args") or [])`. Spot-verified by running the gate that
crashed it — `validate_selection_is_exposed.py` → **PASS**, 42 pages scanned, 19 using `role="tab"`.

**The lesson is the shape, not the key:** a registration schema with optional fields must be read with
`.get()`, or the first entry that exercises the option takes down every gate behind it — and a validator
harness that cannot finish converts *all* of its passes into no evidence at all.

a full board is mid-run: editing those two files would leave their gate reports inconsistent with their
