#### The three "neither" resolved — two are my harness, one is a mild trust claim

**`hive.html` — the premise does not hold there, and that is correct behaviour.** It rendered
*"Pablo Aguilar · Lucena Pharmaceutical Mfg. · SUPERVISOR … 3 areas need you. 30 assets have overdue
PMs."* — full data for a hive the walk had supposedly removed him from. The explanation was already in
this document: **only `hive.html` and `index.html` WRITE `wh_active_hive_id`.** hive.html is the hive
board and picker; it re-resolves real membership and repairs the bogus id, which is exactly what it
should do. The walk cannot put hive.html into the removed state by injecting localStorage, so its result
says nothing about the oracle. Testing it needs an actually-revoked membership.

**`project-report.html` — a paramless arrival, not a boundary.** It showed *"Open this page from the
Project Manager (Detail → Print Report)"*, its correct no-`?project_id=` state. This repo already
recorded the lesson (`a_paramless_walk_is_a_different_page`, learned on this very page) and my harness
walked it paramless anyway. Its boundary behaviour is untested; the walk needs the param.

**`assistant.html` — the one substantive note, and it is a trust claim rather than an empty state.**
It renders *"Your hive — Answers are grounded in this hive's live data: open alerts, overdue …"* while
the viewer can read none of that hive's data. The scope chip promises grounding that RLS is quietly
withholding, so the assistant would answer from an empty context while telling the user it is grounded
in their hive. Smaller than "All clear", same family: **a claim about data made at a moment the platform
cannot see it.** Belongs with the next batch.

**So the arc's honest coverage is 17 surfaces: 5 fixed and verified, 5 already correct, 2 correct by
design (per-person data), 2 newly found and deferred to the next wave, 2 untestable by this harness
(hive, project-report), and 1 trust-claim note (assistant).**

#### ★project-report was CORRECT all along — my vocabulary missed it for the FIFTH time

Walked with its param (`?project_id=`), project-report renders:

> *"Either this project was deleted, or it belongs to a hive your account is not a member of **(this page
> can't tell which)**."*

That is the best answer on the platform, because it is the only one that admits the **ambiguity**: under
RLS a deleted row and a refused row are genuinely indistinguishable from the client, and this page says
so rather than picking one and sounding certain. It was scored "neither" because my pattern knew *"no
longer a member"* and not *"not a member of"*.

**Fifth vocabulary widening, same direction every time — pessimistic.** The regex has now missed
`needs a hive`, `Create or join a Hive`, `does not have access`, centrally-provided copy, and
`not a member of`. Every correction found a surface that was already doing the right thing. That is the
signature of an instrument measuring its author, and it is why the WALK's stable four (later zero) was
the trustworthy number while the census swung 25 → 1.

#### ★engineering-design was a FALSE POSITIVE — and report-sender was already the best of them

Reading the two "deferred defects" before fixing them corrected one and shrank the other.

**engineering-design is not a defect.** The walk matched *"No Report Yet"*, which is the
**pre-calculation placeholder**: `engineering-design.html:713-717` — *"📐 No Report Yet — Fill in the
inputs on the left and click **Run Calculation** to generate your report."* It is the initial state of an
empty report pane, shown to everyone before they run anything, and has nothing to do with a hive
boundary. A string match is not a state; the sixth time this session that reading the code changed the
verdict.

**report-sender is real, and it was already modelling MORE states than anything else on the platform**
(`:1045-1062`): `!_rsContactsSettled` → *"Checking your saved contacts…"* with an em-dash rather than a
zero; `_rsReadFailed` → *"Could not load your contacts. **Unknown right now, not zero.** Reload before
adding one."*; plus a saved-copy fallback variant that says the data may be out of date. Its own comment
records the measurement that produced them: *"Measured under a 500: this card read 'Saved contacts 0 · No
contacts saved yet, add one above · START'."*

The one case it could not see is the read that **settles** with zero because RLS filtered it — so a
removed member is told *"No contacts saved yet, add one above"*: an instruction to fix a problem they do
not have, about a hive they are no longer in. Fixed with the same shared probe and a fourth branch
(`NOT SHOWN`, em-dash, matching the card's own vocabulary for "not a number I can state").

**And the re-render bug repeated itself.** I first wired the probe to call `renderCards()` — a function
that does not exist. It sat inside a `try/catch`, so nothing would have thrown and nothing would have
re-rendered; the card would keep its settled-zero text and the fix would exist only in the source. The
real function is `renderReportSenderSummary()`. **Second time in one batch** that a flag was set without
a working re-render (community was the first) — the failure is silent by construction, which is exactly
why it happened twice.

#### The 34 rows are NOT bankable from this walk — the oracle is shared, the SUBJECTS are not

The obvious last step was to bank all 34 `boundary_not_emptiness` rows against the walk. Reading the rows
stopped that, and the reason is worth more than the banking would have been.

**Each surface carries two rows with different subjects**, and the oracle text they share hides it:

- `PB-<page>-097-CH-ufai-I-**IA**-…` — subject varies per page: *anon (what a stranger sees)* on
  achievements, community, engineering-design and index; *worker (tenant boundary)* on alert-hub,
  analytics and asset-hub; *worker (role floor)* on hive; *worker (own-plan boundary)* on dayplanner.
- `PB-<page>-102-CH-ufai-I-**IB**-…` — **`two_context`** scenarios entirely: dismissal scope, FMEA edit
  race, planning race, citation reachability, cross-member visibility.

**The walk proved exactly one subject:** a signed-in worker whose active hive is one they are not a
member of. That is *"worker (tenant boundary)"* and nothing else. It says nothing about what an **anon**
stranger sees, nothing about a **role floor**, and nothing about any **two-context race** — those need an
anon session and a second browser context respectively.

So banking all 34 would attach evidence to rows whose subject it never touched — the precise failure the
bank's typed evidence exists to prevent, and one `bank_page_walk`'s `classify()` would not catch, because
the row would be structurally valid and merely **untrue**.

**What the walk legitimately supports** is the `worker (tenant boundary)` subset on the surfaces it
covered, and even there `dayplanner`'s row reads *"own-plan boundary"* — the personal data that is
correctly still visible — while the walk exercised its **plant rail**. Different claim, same row id.

**Deferred on purpose, with the shape of the work named:** the anon rows need the harness run with
`signIn(ctx,'anon')`; the `two_context` rows need the paired-context harness this repo already has (the
one used for cross-tenant subscriptions and the moderation three-context walk). Both are real units;
neither is "re-run what I just ran with a different flag".

#### The anon subject, walked — all four correct

`--anon` mode added (skip sign-in, inject no hive id — a stranger has neither). It is a **different
subject**, not the same walk with a flag: a stranger is refused because there is no JWT at all, where a
removed member is refused because the JWT's membership was revoked. The `-097-IA` rows on achievements,
community, engineering-design and index all read *"anon (what a stranger sees)"*, so they needed this.

```
ok  achievements   <- "Join the Hive"      ok  engineering-design <- "Join the Hive"
ok  community      <- "Join the Hive"      ok  index              <- "Join the Hive"

4 surfaces walked as an ANONYMOUS stranger · 0 answer with EMPTINESS
```

**All four already name the boundary** — a stranger is offered the join path rather than shown an empty
dashboard. Nothing to fix; the evidence is what those four rows were waiting for.

The summary line was also corrected: it printed *"walked as a removed member"* in anon mode, which is the
same class of error as the harness naming the wrong output file — **a report that misstates its own
subject is worse than no report**, because the number looks like evidence for a claim it never tested.

**Remaining on the arc:** the `two_context` (`-102-IB`) rows — dismissal scope, FMEA edit race, planning
race, citation reachability, cross-member visibility — need the paired-context harness this repo already
has. And `hive`'s *"role floor"* row needs a genuinely revoked membership from the seeder.

> contains a UTF-8 `·` that my match string did not reproduce, so the assertion threw and nothing was

> becoming a false report, the exact shape already in the memory bank. It is now genuinely fixed and
> re-run — `1 surfaces walked as an ANONYMOUS stranger` — but the ordering was wrong: **verify, then
> record.** Writing the claim first is how a document drifts from the code it describes.

#### The `two_context` rows already have their harness — `tests/marketplace-bank-two-context.spec.ts`

Recalled rather than rebuilt. The file exists for exactly this shape, and its own header states the rule
this arc needs:

> *"Every existing spec in this repo drives ONE signed-in identity… A handoff between two parties cannot
> be proven from one browser: the whole point is that what A does appears to B. So this file exists to
> hold role-PAIR cells. Two independent browser contexts, two real Supabase Auth sessions, one shared row
> of truth in between."*

It also fixes the ALTITUDE for the `-102-IB` rows, and getting that right is most of the work:

> *"The data path is already banked in SQL… What SQL cannot prove is that the client's screen repaints,
> and a silent subscription failure looks exactly like a provider who has not moved. That is the only
> thing this spec asserts, so it stays small — the pyramid's UI layer should be."*

**So the remaining five `two_context` subjects each reduce to one small UI assertion**, because their data
paths are already proven in psql: alert-hub *dismissal scope* (does A's dismissal reach B's screen, or is
it A's alone?), asset-hub *FMEA edit race*, dayplanner *planning race*, assistant *citation reachability*,
hive *cross-member visibility*. Each is "what A does appears (or correctly does NOT appear) to B" — not a
new harness, a new cell in an existing one.

**And `hive`'s "role floor" row needs the seeder**, not a harness: the walk cannot inject its way into a
revoked membership because hive.html correctly re-resolves and repairs the id. A genuinely kicked member
(`hive_members.status = 'kicked'`) is a seeder fixture, and `test-data-seeder/` already writes membership
rows.

That is the whole remainder of the arc, with the machinery named for each piece.

Ian's push (*"why is it the third are mine? can you just be proactive"*) was correct three times over.

### ★THE SCOREBOARD WAS FLATTERING — six rows disagreed with their own basis, every one inflated

Being proactive on the registry turned up drift the anti-drift gate could not see. A basis is
**append-only**: a later pass often revises the number in prose (`"pct -> 72"`) and only the PROSE is
updated, leaving the pct FIELD holding an older, higher value.

| | field said | its own basis said | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T121** shared device | 99 | **78** | +21 |
| **T147** optimistic UI | 95 | **72** | +23 |
| T47 KPI hand-check | 95 | 88 | +7 |
| T78 nav-hub spine | 90 | 84 | +6 |
| T169 bot defense | 86 | 80 | +6 |
| T129 1000-entry logbook | 99 | 98 | +1 |

**Six found, six inflated, none deflated** — which is the direction drift always takes when nothing is
checking. T147 is the sharpest: its basis says *"A real registry needs a discriminator keyed to WHAT is
painted… which the next pass owes. pct -> 72"* — a deliberate DOWNGRADE the field ignored, leaving the
row claiming 95.

Rules 2 and 5 could not catch this. They check `status -> pct` and gate registration; neither asks
whether a row **agrees with its own account of itself**.

**Fixed both ways:** the six fields corrected (program 86.8% → **86.5%**, honestly lower), and
`validate_trajectory_registry.py` gains **rule 6 — pct must match the basis's own last `pct -> N`**.
Teeth proven by re-inflating T121 to 99: `FAIL T121: pct field 99 disagrees with its own basis, which
last says pct -> 78 (update the field, or the number flatters)`.

**This is the same lesson as the Ian-gated miscount, one layer down:** a basis is a narrative, and
*matching* it is not *reading* it. The 60-item list came from matching a request and ignoring its answer;
this drift came from writing an answer and ignoring the field. Both were caught by reading what the
record actually says — and both were flattering before they were caught.

### ★THE "3 KNOWN FAILURES" WAS A FAST BOARD — 405 of 1019 gates were SKIPPED

Pre-checking the closure batch against the board on disk turned up something worse than the batch's own
state. `platform_health.json` reads:

```
mode: fast · PASS 611 · FAIL 3 · SKIP 405 · duration 790s
```

**Forty percent of the board did not run.** And the skipped set is not incidental — **every gate all
sixteen closure-batch trajectories depend on is in it**: `flow-fits-the-floor`, `dialog-floor`,
`chain-journey`, `kpi-parity`, `hive-at-scale`, `print-is-readable-on-paper`, `a-secret-stays-masked`,
`draft-survives-reauth`, `selection-is-exposed`, all of them **SKIP**.

**So the "3 known failures" I have been quoting all session is a partial picture**, and I should have
read `mode` before quoting it. Those three (`substrate-freshness`, `clone-debt`, `ai-asset-versioning`)
are the failures *among the 611 that ran* — the other 405 have no recent verdict at all.

**This is the `KeyError: 'args'` crash's real cost, and it is larger than "the restamp was blocked."**
`skip_if_fast` gates only run on a FULL board; the full board has been dying 66 minutes in on an
unguarded dict key. So the expensive half of the verification — every live walk, every browser prover,
every gate too slow for the fast lane — **has not completed in a long time**, and the fast board that
kept passing looked like coverage while carrying 405 unrun gates.

**Which makes the board now running the first complete verification in that whole window**, and the
thing every one of the 16 closures is waiting on. It is at 318 reports and past the crash point.

**The lesson generalises beyond this program:** a board that reports `611 PASS · 3 FAIL` and a board that
reports `611 PASS · 3 FAIL · 405 SKIP` are different claims, and only one of them is coverage. A summary
line that omits the skip count is the same class as a row cap shown as a total.

### ★AND THE LOCKS REST ON THE SAME SKIPPED GATES — 16 of the 20 at 100%

The SKIP finding has a sharper edge. Checking the **locked** trajectories' gates against that same board:

| | locked trajectories |
|---|---|
| every gate PASSed on that board | **1** |
| some gates skipped | 3 |
| **ALL gates skipped** | **16** |

T6 and T7 (the invite-code round trip — the most load-bearing flow on the platform), T8 (re-auth
restore), T11 (stock ripple), T14 (offline queue drain), T15 (fault search), T28 (audit reachability),
T45 (Filipino), T166 (composer audience), T176 (error taxonomy) — all sitting at **100%**, all resting on
gates that read **SKIP**.

**What is FACT and what is INFERENCE, kept apart:**
- **Fact:** the only board on disk is `mode: fast`; those gates are `skip_if_fast`, so they did not run on it.
- **Fact:** full boards have been dying 66 minutes in on `KeyError: 'args'` until today's fix.
- **Fact:** `baseline_ref` is **2026-08-23**, eight days old, and no archived health snapshots exist.
- **Inference, stated as one:** those gates' last full-board verdict therefore predates the crash, and
  **the artifacts on disk cannot say when it was.** SKIP does not mean a gate never passed — it means
  nothing on disk shows it passing recently.

**This does not say the locks are wrong. It says they are UNVERIFIED, which is a different and quieter
problem** — and it is exactly the shape this bank already records twice today: a lock nothing runs locks
nothing, and a green summary that omits its skip count is not coverage.

**The board running now is the first thing in this window that can settle it.** When it lands it does
three jobs at once: freshen the reports for the restamp, give the 16-row closure batch its verdicts, and
**re-verify the 16 existing locks** that have been asserting 100% on gates nobody has watched run.

**A clean negative worth recording:** the 405 skips are *exactly* the 405 gates marked `skip_if_fast` —
checked by parsing the registration source and differencing the sets, `skipped - skip_if_fast = 0`. **No
gate skips for a hidden reason**, so the worse version of this finding (a gate that skips on every board
and therefore runs never) does not exist. The skipped set is legitimate and well-defined: it is the slow
and live half of the board, which only a FULL run exercises — and the full run is what has been dying.

### The drift audit's mirror: understatement — and why only ONE row was advanced

Having found six rows claiming a pct their basis did not support, I looked for the opposite. **75 of the
116 `fixing` rows already name a registered gate, and 47 of them contain an explicit assertion that the
lock is built** — *"Locked as 'trust-claim-backed'"*, *"LOCKED BY gate"*, *"gate timed-journey-family
registered"* — while the status still reads `fixing`. The validator's own rule 5 says **`locking` MEANS
the lock exists**, so on the face of it 47 rows are understated.

**Only one was advanced, and the reason is the discipline itself.** "Locked as X" in these bases almost
always means *one FINDING* of the trajectory is gated, not that the trajectory's lock is complete — a
trajectory can gate a property it fixed early while real work continues, which is exactly what `fixing`
is for. Bulk-promoting 47 rows on a phrase match would be **the same error as the 60-item Ian list**: a
pattern read as a claim. It would also inflate the program in the direction the pct audit just corrected.

**T118 was advanced because its basis leaves no ambiguity:** *"Remaining: nothing owed beyond the
wave-close re-earn — idle-network, reduced-motion and the 4x CPU lane are all measured."* Gate registered,
prover on disk, nothing else owed. `fixing -> locking`, **pct held at 96** — status is not evidence, and
the re-earn is still owed. (fixing 116 → 115, locking 62 → 63.)

**What this leaves is a real definitional problem, recorded rather than papered over:** the
`fixing`/`locking` boundary is being applied inconsistently across 47 rows, because "the lock exists" is
ambiguous between *a* lock and *the* lock. The durable fix is to make `locking` mean something checkable —
e.g. every finding the basis names carries a registered gate — which is a rule-6-shaped addition to the
validator rather than 47 hand judgements. **Not attempted today**: the board is mid-run, and a status
sweep of that size wants its own pass with the re-earn already landed.

#### The closure batch is staged as a driver that REFUSES on bad evidence

`<scratchpad>/close_batch.py` (staged while the board ran; belongs in `tools/` once the run is clear).
It advances the sixteen to `locked` only when **both** conditions hold:

1. `platform_health.json` is **not** `mode: fast` — a fast board SKIPs 405 gates and every gate this
   batch depends on is in that set, so a fast board can never license these closes; and
2. every gate the trajectory names reads **PASS** on that board.

Otherwise it prints `KEEP <id> gate not green: ...` and closes nothing. Dry-run by default.

**Its guard is already proven, which is the point of staging it:** run against today's on-disk board it
answers

```
REFUSED: platform_health.json is mode='fast'. 405 gates SKIP on a fast board and every gate this
batch depends on is among them - a fast board cannot license these closes.
```

Sixteen hand-edits would be sixteen chances to advance a row whose gate had gone red — which is exactly
the flattery the pct audit found six instances of today. A driver that refuses is cheaper than a
judgement repeated sixteen times.

### ★AN ORPHANED GATE: T85 locked on something the board never ran

Chasing the understatement question turned up a phantom lock. **T85** (`locking`, 90% — companion persona
switching) names `companion-delivery` in its artifacts. That gate:

- **exists** — `tools/companion_delivery_gate.py`
- **passes** — run standalone: `PASS persona_resolution current=0 baseline=0`
- **was registered ZERO times in `run_platform_checks.py`**

So the registry asserted a lock, the script existed, the script passed — and **nothing connected the
three**. The board had never executed it.

**Rule 5's hole let it stand.** That rule was strengthened on 2026-08-26 precisely because *"LOCKING MEANS
THE GATE IS BUILT, so it must name one"* — but it checks a gate is **named**, and for `locked` that the
name **resolves**; for `locking` it never resolves the name. One row exploited exactly that gap. Audited:
**T85 is the only one** — every other locked/locking row's gates resolve (T1's
`link-target-existence(upgraded)` is fine; rule 5 splits at `(` and the base is registered).

**Fixed by registering it**, which is the whole repair — the gate was already correct.

**★THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS TODAY, and the three are indistinguishable from outside:**

| | how the lock was hollow | found by |
|---|---|---|
| 96 psql recipes | carried a `replay` line; **nothing re-ran them** | converting bank rows |
| 16 of 20 locked trajectories | gates read **SKIP** — full boards were dying on `KeyError: 'args'` | pre-checking the closure batch |
| **T85** | gate **never registered** | auditing understatement |

**Unregistered, unrun, and skipped all look exactly like green.** That is why "a lock nothing runs locks
nothing" needed a mechanical check rather than a slogan.

**New instrument, staged:** `<scratchpad>/validate_locks_are_verified.py` asserts that every
`locked`/`locking` row's gates read **PASS on a FULL board**. Both behaviours proven — **PASS** against a
synthetic full board (83 rows), and **UNVERIFIABLE** (not OK, exit 1 under `--strict`) against today's
real board, because *"a lock's gate cannot be confirmed from a board that did not run it, and reporting
OK here would be the exact silence this check exists to break."* It also normalises gate ids the same way
rule 5 does — a mismatch there produced a false positive, which is how the normalisation was noticed:
**two checkers reading one field by different rules will always eventually disagree.**

### ★THE ORPHAN AUDIT: 629 gate-shaped scripts, 6 that nothing runs

T85's phantom lock was not unique, so the question was asked of every instrument in the repo rather than
only the ones the registry names.

**629** gate-shaped scripts (`validate_*.py`, `prove_*.mjs`, `prove_*.py`, `*_gate.py`). **96** are absent
from `run_platform_checks.py` — but that alone proves nothing, because most `prove_*.mjs` files are
invoked BY a `validate_*.py` wrapper. Removing everything referenced anywhere else leaves **9**, and
three of those are superseded near-twins:

- `prove_offline_queue_survives_restart.mjs` — superseded by `prove_queue_survives_restart.mjs`, which the
  registered `queue-survives-restart` gate really does run. **T14's lock is sound** — checked, because a
  near-identical filename is exactly how a good lock gets mistaken for a hollow one.
- `prove_session_expiry_registry.mjs`, `prove_view_inputs.mjs` — same pattern.

**Six are genuinely unrun, and each was built for a named trajectory:**

| prover | belongs to |
|---|---|
| `prove_sw_two_version_transition.mjs` | T44 installed-PWA / T192 release day |
| `prove_mid_migration_writes.py` | T199 the migration window |
| `prove_jargon_is_glossed.mjs` | T177 vocabulary census |
| `prove_throttled_first_paint.mjs` | T37 slow-3G |
| `prove_availability_pages.mjs` | T102 provider availability |
| **`prove_anon_boundaries.py`** | the anon threat model |

**`anon-boundaries` is registered as of today, because it ran and passed 3/3** — and it is a security
prover nobody was running. It asks what a signed-in probe structurally cannot: **BOLA** (an unpublished
listing that EXISTS, fetched by id as anon → 200 with 0 rows — a refusal, not an empty table), **JWT not
body** (an anon INSERT claiming a `seller_name` in the payload → 401 from the policy), and **tenant
boundary as a SET** (all 7 unpublished listings across every hive in ONE anon query → 0 visible).

The other five are browser or migration provers; running them now would contend with the board (and
`prove_mid_migration_writes` applies migrations, which is not a mid-board activity). **Recorded as the
next registration batch, each with its trajectory named.**

**Three ways a lock can be hollow, all found today, all identical from outside:** the gate is
**unregistered** (T85, anon-boundaries), the gate is **unrun** (96 psql recipes), or the gate is
**skipped** (405 on a fast board). None of them looks different from green until someone asks a question
the board itself cannot answer.

to `run_platform_checks.py` today — in a file whose last defect was a malformed registration that killed

```
  anon-boundaries          tools/prove_anon_boundaries.py        severity=fail

  psql-probe-suite         tools/validate_psql_probe_suite.py    severity=fail
```

**The first pass of that check reported "32 scripts missing on disk" and it was wrong** — my parser
mapped non-literal `script` values to the string `'<expr>'`, which naturally is not a file. Re-run
properly: **991 literal paths, 0 missing**, and 32 entries that build their path from an expression.

Trivial in itself, and worth one line because of the tally: today an instrument was wrong rather than the
code in the census (25 → 1), the Ian-gated count (60 → 11), the walk vocabulary (five widenings), the
`\b`-as-backspace bytes, the "T14 lock is hollow" near-miss, and now this. **The code was wrong four
times; the instrument was wrong nine.** Which is the argument for checking the instrument first, every
time — not a counsel of despair about instruments.
